articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.
Editorial Context: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

Editorial Context: Core accountability: On core sector performance. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

Core accountability: On core sector performance

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency.
The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour.
The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu.
Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back.

A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented. “Under the Act, the Nellore Collector, should have issued notice to the boat owners, summoned them and made them pay the requisite fine. However, this has not been done.”
Also, no action has been taken by the Andhra Pradesh government on the boats from Karaikal that had fished close to their coast.
“The fishermen from Karaikal were the ones who had escaped along with their boats that were impounded in Andhra Pradesh,” said another source.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 23 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency.

The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour.

The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu.

Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back.

A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented. “Under the Act, the Nellore Collector, should have issued notice to the boat owners, summoned them and made them pay the requisite fine. However, this has not been done.”

Also, no action has been taken by the Andhra Pradesh government on the boats from Karaikal that had fished close to their coast.

“The fishermen from Karaikal were the ones who had escaped along with their boats that were impounded in Andhra Pradesh,” said another source.

articles.title: Over 4,850 buses, 16 special trains to run for Karthigai Deepam in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh inspects civic and security arrangements made for devotees ahead of the festival
Sixteen special trains and 4,877 buses will be operated to Tiruvannamalai town from November 23-25 as part of Karthigai Deepam festival.

On Sunday, Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S. Ramesh inspected civic and security arrangements made for devotees ahead of the festival, including Maha Deepam (November 24). District Collector Vandhana Garg was also present.

“More than 15,500 police personnel will be deployed in the town for security purposes. Around 1,100 CCTV cameras including 556 surveillance box cameras have also been roped as part of safety measures,” Mr. Ramesh said.

The district administration has set up 26 temporary bus termini, mostly on the outskirts of the town, with 26 diesel-run generators. The transport department will operate 160 free shuttle services between the temporary bus termini and various parts of the town, including the 14-km Girivalam path and Arunachaleswarar Temple. As per estimates, around 50 lakh devotees are expected for the festival.

As part of annadanam (distribution of free food), 288 spots were allotted for volunteers to distribute free food to visitors. Seven food safety testing teams will monitor the quality of the food distributed in these spots.
All private vehicles, including tourist cabs, are prohibited from entering the town to provide more road space for walkers to reach the temple. It will help to prevent congestion and stampedes.

Vehicles can be parked at any of the 155 parking lots that are away from the town, where over 21,000 vehicles can be parked. Jute mats will be laid for at least a distance of two km on the footpaths to allow visitors to walk to the temple safely. Children at the festival will be given wristbands to ensure their safety.

The health department has set up 120 medical camps, mostly on the Girivalam path and bus terminuses, for the festival. Around 35 ambulances including 10 bike ambulances, have also been roped. Adequate water taps (146 spots), washrooms (600 spots), and 10,900 streetlights have been set up for the festival. A total of 2,466 sanitation staff were roped in to keep the town clean of trash.

To ensure the safety of visitors, 31 police watch towers that will be supported by 350 bike patrols and 62 help desks in the town round the clock. Around 110 firefighters with 26 water tenders will be deployed to prevent accidental fires, especially on the hillock during Maha Deepam. For emergencies during the festival, helpline numbers are: 04175-233344; 04175-233345; 8072797683.

articles.title: Palarivattom SHO suspended over alleged links with accused in forgery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The station house officer (SHO) of the Palarivattom police was suspended on Sunday (November 22) over his alleged links with Rajendran Vellappalath, chairman of the Kerala Pravasi Association, who has been arrested in a major forgery case.

Inspector Manjith Lal was suspended by District Police Chief (Kochi City) R. Nishanthini pending an inquiry, based on an internal report which found prima facie irregularities and a serious violation of discipline, as per the suspension order.

Mr. Manjith Lal is accused of establishing an unauthorised connection with Mr. Vellappalath and using WhatsApp to share details of the case that the Angamaly police had registered against Mr. Vellappalath. The inspector also allegedly shared details of the Indian Cooperative Credit Society Ltd and its key officials with Mr. Vellappalath at his request. The WhatsApp messages were deleted from the inspector’s phone soon after the Ernakulam Rural Crime Branch arrested Mr. Vellappalath on November 12, the suspension order stated.

An assistant commissioner with the Kochi City Crime Branch has been tasked with investigating the allegations against Mr. Manjith Lal and submitting a report within two months. Earlier, the police had searched the Palarivattom police station and seized the inspector’s phone as part of the probe.

articles.title: Congress leaders from Keralam urge AICC to restore consultations within party ahead of UDF’s policy decisions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: K.C. Joseph, Benny Behanan, Shafi Parambil meet Mallikarjun Kharge, air grievances about a 'dormant' party apparatus stemming from the lack of a full-time State president and delayed reorganisation. Their demands include a hands-on party president

Top Congress leaders from arguably “rival factions” are seeking the All India Congress Committee (AICC)’s intervention to address what they see as a lack of consultation, which they contend makes consensus elusive when the United Democratic Front (UDF) government decides policy and pushes key political appointments.

Veteran Congress leader K.C. Joseph; Benny Behanan, MP; and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) working president Shafi Parambil are the latest among the top Keralam leaders to go to New Delhi to ostensibly air their grievances about a “dormant” party apparatus stemming, chiefly, from the lack of a full-time State president and “delayed” reorganisation.

Notably, Mr. Behanan is also among the top four contenders for the KPCC president post, with the incumbent and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph demanding that he be relieved of the job so he can focus solely on his Cabinet responsibilities. Others in the race include Congress Working Committee (CWC) president Kodikunnil Suresh, Joseph Vazhakkan, and Ajay Tharayil.

Mr. K.C. Joseph told The Hindu that the trio had met AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge. “The KPCC office is largely deserted these days. The desolation telegraphs an atrophied, almost moribund party machinery to the rank-and-file. A hands-on party president and swift reorganisation from the top down is the only panacea to the torpor that has beset the Congress in Kerala,” he said. Mr. Joseph said the meeting was “anything but about censuring any person or apportioning blame”. He said the party and the government have to march in lockstep.

“We have demanded the constitution of a party committee to look into impending appointments to boards and corporations earmarked for Congress workers. The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) has a similar structure,” Mr. Joseph said.

Another Congress insider said the demand for organisational restructuring and institution of a consultative mechanism to weigh policy and key nominations was gaining ground in the party in Kerala. He said many leaders feared that the delay in rectifying the current “organisational lacunae” could feed factionalism.

Months earlier, United Democratic Front (UDF) convener Adoor Prakash, MP, had met Mr. Kharge and complained about the lack of consultation in the ruling alliance, which he said had rendered the apex political structure redundant.

Mr. Joseph’s visit also came as the Left Democratic Front (LDF) accused Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of bypassing the Cabinet and the UDF, leaving key decision-making to a “power group” centred on the Cabinet. Notably, Mr. Joseph, Mr. Behanan and Mr. Parambil, widely regarded as leaders of the so-called “A-group” in the KPCC, had met Mr. Satheesan earlier and raised the same demands.

fullParagraphs: Only 83,972 voters have been included in the electoral rolls after the SIR. Many residents of rental accommodation say they need assistance for inclusion. Officials point to lack of awareness among the residents of the SIR

Most of the 12.22 lakh electors, whose names were removed during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Chennai district after they were classified as “permanently shifted”, are yet to apply for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.

According to estimates, 51% of the residents in Chennai own a house, while 49% live in rental accommodation. Many electors who shifted their residence before the 2026 Assembly election complained that they did not vote this year as their names were removed from the rolls. However, only 83,972 voters in the city have been included in the rolls after the SIR. Many residents of rental accommodation have said they need assistance for including their names in the rolls.

B. Raja, who is living in rental accommodation, was an elector under a polling booth at Chintadripet in the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni Assembly Constituency until the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This Assembly election, he visited the polling booth, but was not permitted to vote because his name was removed during the SIR after he shifted to another house in the city.

“Many residents like me who have to shift to new rental houses frequently could not vote in the Assembly election at our booth because we did not know what to do. We may need assistance. Once we start visiting a government office, we have to spend a lot of time,” he said.

Officials point to lack of awareness among the residents of the SIR. Not many residents who lost their votes visited the camps conducted by the Chennai District Election Office on Sunday (November 22, 2026) for inclusion of their names in the rolls.

Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said, “Wide publicity has been given to the camps [held on Sunday]. Furthermore, this process is continuous. Online applications can also be used. We will again cross-check the absent, shifted voters, as emerged during the SIR, and ensure that no eligible voters are left out of the rolls... Electoral camps in colleges will be part of this drive.”

“After the SIR, multiple rounds of opportunities have been given to eligible voters to become part of the rolls. As many as 83,972 voters have been included in the rolls since the final electoral rolls came out after the SIR, and the draft roll was published for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) on November 12. We will hold special camps again on November 29. Enough publicity has been given to that too,” Dr. Sameeran said.

“Another way to publicise it is through Booth Level Agents (BLAs). We have created awareness at our meetings with political parties. We have not received any major claim and objection or complaint from members of the public about denial of opportunity to register their names. Nevertheless, we will intensify voter registration during this SSR. Residents have been requested to lodge complaints with the District Election Office with details so that we can find solutions,” Dr. Sameeran said.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

fullParagraphs: Takshashila University conferred honorary doctorates upon Tamil author and screenwriter S. Ramakrishnan and playback singer K.S. Chithra at its second convocation held at Ongur in Tindivanam recently.
According to a press note, the University awarded gold medals to 19 students and recognised 186 students who secured first class with distinction.
In his address, M. Dhanasekaran, University Chancellor underscored the role of quality education, perseverance, discipline and moral values in shaping responsible citizens.

articles.title: Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.
Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident.
Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction.

“Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added.

Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist.
The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly.

“Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.
Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said an FIR was lodged against the minors under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the BNS.
All of them were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and notices were sent to their parents.

According to the police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of minors surrounded them and began to abuse them. When the couple tried to reason with the group, they assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden. Police detained them after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.
The police said they are recording the statements of the couple and the juveniles to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident that took place at the Pramod Mahajan Garden.

The incident drew sharp reactions from political parties, with many condemning it. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra president Abu Asim Azmi said the juvenile age threshold should be brought down from 18 to 15 and that those below 18 years who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not be given concessions under the law. Mr. Azmi added that the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.
Meanwhile, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya met the couple at the Ghatkopar police station and promised action.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 23 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said an FIR was lodged against the minors under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the BNS.

All of them were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and notices were sent to their parents.

According to the police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of minors surrounded them and began to abuse them. When the couple tried to reason with the group, they assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden. Police detained them after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.

The police said they are recording the statements of the couple and the juveniles to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident that took place at the Pramod Mahajan Garden.

The incident drew sharp reactions from political parties, with many condemning it. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra president Abu Asim Azmi said the juvenile age threshold should be brought down from 18 to 15 and that those below 18 years who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not be given concessions under the law. Mr. Azmi added that the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.

Meanwhile, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya met the couple at the Ghatkopar police station and promised action.

NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the Home portfolio, to “adopt a no-tolerance policy towards such incidents” and said citizens should be able to move around freely in the State.

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the assault.

articles.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department.
Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged.

Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added.

Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests.
Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October.

On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

“The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

articles.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years.
Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls

As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues.
They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary.

As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year.

“The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow.

Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”.

Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances.

“The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.
Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

Editorial Context: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.
In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka.
He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner.

Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added.

articles.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be eligible for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.
The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.
The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.

The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.

“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.

“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.

The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.

While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.

In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.

articles.title: Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs inaugurated in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor on Saturday inaugurated the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C. P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation (CPRAF) to mark the institution’s 60th anniversary.

He also released two books, Heritage, Education and Nature – 60 years of the C.P.Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation, and A catalogue of Ravi Varma’s Oleographs and Chomo Lithographs. Speaking during the launch, Mr. Tharoor, a long-time friend of the family, said as an MP for Thiruvananthapuram, he represented a city and a region whose history is closely connected with both Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer and Raja Ravi Varma. To find their legacies brought together here in Chennai in an institution that has spent 60 years serving the wider public, is a particularly happy conjunction of history.
He said the lithographs of Raja Ravi Varma, while becoming familiar objects across the country, also allowed the many who were barred from entering temples to worship the deities as well.

One of the most significant reforms associated with Sir C.P.’s term as Dewan of Travancore was the temple entry proclamation, he added. He praised the work of the various schools run by the Foundation. including the Saraswathi Kendra in Chennai that was the city’s first school for children with autism, dyslexia and learning disabilities.

Former Madras High Court judge P. N. Prakash, who received the first copies of the books, said that Sir C.P. had a magnetic personality, was a tennis player, and a polyglot who could speak several languages including, French and Latin; and he was the youngest Advocate General of Madras High court.

Chairman and managing director of Seshasayee Paper & Boards Ltd., N. Gopalaratnam, said that Sir C.P. was very close to the Sesashayee Brothers and had helped them to put up FACT, PCC and many other industries. He was instrumental in starting hydroelectric projects including Pykara, Lower Bhavani Scheme and the one at Mettur Dam. “As a schoolboy, I have had the opportunity to watch him speak on two occasions. Though I did not understand everything that he spoke, his image as a majestic, well-dressed man lingers in my mind.”

Elaborating on the work done by the Foundation over the past 60 years, its president Nanditha Krishna said that the C.P. Art Gallery was established as the city’s first craft gallery to creeate a bridge between ancient craftsmanship and contemporary society. The Foundation introduced puppetry as a teaching aid, and trained and encouraged women. It established The Grove School, Rangammal Vidyalaya in Kancheepuram and the Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar Memorial School in Kumbakonam. Its Each One Teach One Initiative, launched by Shakuntala Jagannathan, in 1997, provides scholarships to children.
Prashanth Krishna, director of CPRAF and senior advocate and grandson of Sir C.P., Aryama Sundaram spoke.

articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will; the demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA rigging; this fight isn’t over,’ said a protester

Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.
Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.
“Students, who have worked hard, deserve justice. We have already ordered an inquiry to identify the irregularities, and action will follow if evidence is found,” said Ms. Firdous.

The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.

Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”

The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.

On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.

Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.

“Students, who have worked hard, deserve justice. We have already ordered an inquiry to identify the irregularities, and action will follow if evidence is found,” said Ms. Firdous.

articles.title: Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has urged Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Supreme Court Collegium to urgently recommend a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak , who is due to retire on November 27.

In a letter to CJI and Judges of the Collegium, Mr. Soren pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.

“As the Head of the State Government, I am compelled to draw your attention to the fact that an incoming Chief Justice has not been designated nor has any Justice been transferred to the Jharkhand High Court in advance as envisaged under the MoP’ and the Collegium’s statement of February 26, 2026 to assume charge as the Chief Justice on the superannuation of Chief Justice M.S. Sonak on Number 27, 2026,” Mr. Soren wrote in the letter dated November 12, 2026, however shared with media on late night Saturday (November 21, 2026).
He added that the judiciary in the guardian of the Indian Constitution and it serves as the “custodian of Individual liberties and ensures that the rule of law prevails”
Mr. Soren expressed concern that High Court needs stable functioning and regular judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the administration of justice.

He cited the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) for appointment of Chief Justices of High Courts which lays down time bound safeguards requiring appointments to be finalised in advance and strictly limiting the tenure of an Acting Chief Justice to ensure that High Courts do not suffer from a leadership vacuum.
He also mentioned that paragraph 3 of the MoP says that initiation of the proposal for the appointment of Chief Justice of a High Court would be by the CJI.
He added that the process of appointment must be initiated well in time to ensure the completion at least one month prior to the date of anticipated vacancy for the Chief Justice of the High Court.

“The CJI would ensure that when a Chief Justice is transferred from one High Court to another simultaneous appointment of his successor in office should be made and ordinarily the arrangement of appointment of an acting Chief justice should not be made for more than one month,” Mr. Soren wrote in the letter.
Jharkhand CM asserted that the High Court of Jharkhand has repeatedly experienced short leadership tenures and interim Acting Chief Justice arrangements at the helm.

“Prior to the appointment of the incumbent Chief Justice, Justice M.S. Sonak on January 9, 2026, the Jharkhand High Court has been adorned by four Chief Justice since the superannuation of Justice Ravi Ranjan on December 19.2022, one of the lordships having a term of a fortnight. During this period, Acting Chief Justices have been appointed on three occasions for terms ranging from two months to six months,” Mr. Soren said.
He also expressed concern that without the Collegium’s immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement.
