articles.title: Man sentenced to 10 year rigorous imprisonment for raping home-alone woman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Convict Anil Poojary, resident of Sangabettu, was also sentenced to one year simple imprisonment with a fine of ₹1,000 for the offences of tresspass, criminal intimidation and other offences

An additional district and sessions court in Mangaluru convicted a 30 year-old man from Bantwal taluk for the offence of rape and sentenced him to 10 year rigorous imprisonment along with ₹50,000 fine on Saturday, November 21.

Convict Anil Poojary, resident of Sangabettu, was also sentenced to one year simple imprisonment with a fine of ₹1,000 for the offences of tresspass, criminal intimidation and other offences by VI Additional District and Sessions Judge Rajesh Maruthi Kamathe, according to Public Prosecutor Chowdhury Motilal, who led the prosecution in the case.

Poojary on August 11, 2021, had entered the house of the victim, home-alone woman in the same village during the evening and assaulted her. Later, he dragged the victim inside her house and raped her between 6.30 p.m. and 8.30 p.m. before threatening her with dire consequences if she revealed the incident to others.

Bantwal rural police had registered a case and probed the matter. While Police Sub Inspector M. S. Prasanna and team nabbed the accused, Police Inspector T. D. Nagaraj investigated the case and initiated the prosecution. Prosecution had produced 30 documents and 14 witnesses for the trial.

On conclusion of the trial, the judge convicted Poojary for the offences mentioned and sentenced him to imprisonment. Out of ₹51,000 fine, ₹50,000 should be paid to the victim, he said besides directing the district legal services authority to pay suitable compensation to her.

articles.title: Indian-origin man detained in Texas after serving sentence for visual recording conviction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Raghul Anandakrishnan's custody has been assumed from a Texas county jail, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a post on November 22

A 29-year-old Indian-origin man has been taken into custody by Federal immigration authorities in Texas following his conviction for attempted invasive visual recording, and he will remain detained while immigration court proceedings are pending, authorities said.
Raghul Anandakrishnan's custody has been assumed from a Texas county jail, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a post on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

In an official post on X , Raghul Anandakrishnan served time in a county jail in Texas after his conviction for attempted invasive visual recording. The conviction came after a woman reported that an employee at a wireless company went through her phone and transferred explicit photos of her from her phone to his.
"ICE took custody of him from the county jail. He'll remain in ICE custody pending immigration court proceedings," the post said.

The detention follows a June criminal case in Austin, where Austin Police Department records and Travis County court filings cited by local media showed Anandakrishnan was arrested while employed at a Total Wireless store.
According to court affidavits, he sent two intimate images from a customer's phone to his own device via AirDrop and accessed the customer's Snapchat account.

Travis County jail records show he was initially booked on June 7 on charges of invasive visual recording and computer security breach under a combined $10,000 bond and placed under no-contact orders before later being convicted of attempted invasive visual recording.
Federal officials have not immediately released details regarding his immigration status, current detention facility, or upcoming immigration court dates.

articles.title: NHAI yet to act despite 300 complaints of inordinate delay at Chowlagere toll plaza on NH 75 Hassan-Sakleshpur section
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Authority says it will raise the issue with Indian Highways Management Company that handles FASTag of vehicles

Road users have alleged frequent delays in clearing of the vehicles, particularly those with annual FASTag at the Chowlagere Toll Plaza on Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and Sakleshpur and rude behaviour by the personnel manning the facility.

Chowlagere toll plaza near Alur in Hassan district is a part of NH 75 four-lane project between Hassan and Maranahalli (about 45 km) executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The four-lane work got completed a couple of years ago with much delay.

Annoyed with the frequent delays faced by him personally, P. Aditya Narayan from Puttur, a regular traveller on the section sought details of similar complaints under the Right to Information Act from the NHAI. For his surprise, a November 20 reply from the Authority informed that as many as 300 complaints were made to the NHAI, 205 through the Rajmarg Yatra Portal and 95 through 1033 NHAI Helpline between April and November 15, 2026.

During the period, three complaints were received about the staff misbehaviour with road users, the Authority said in the reply. Majority of the causes for the delay in lifting of the toll barrier included software problem, connection failure and a few issues of hardware failure, the reply said.

Mr. Narayan said the scanner often took an unusually long time to read the FASTag. “We were forced to wait, honk twice or thrice and eventually the toll staff contact the control room over walkie-talkie, communicate the vehicle number and get the passage cleared manually.”

After he brought the issue to MLC Kishore Kumar’s notice, the legislator wrote to the NHAI to immediately address the issue. Still, the Authority has not rectified the mistake in the system, he regretted.

Janekere Paramesh, a photojournalist from Sakleshpur who often travels to Hassan, endorses the complaints and said ever since the Chowlagere toll plaza was commissioned, road users have been facing problems of delayed clearance. Rude behaviour by the plaza personnel adds to the agony of road users, he said adding en-number of complaints to the Authority have remained unaddressed.
Mr. Narayan further said FASTag annual pass-holders face similar delays in many other toll plazas across the state.

Stating that the NHAI directly does not handle FASTag issues as it was being dealt by Indian Highways Management Company Ltd., Authority’s Karnataka Regional Officer V P Brahmankar told The Hindu that he would raise the issue with its CEO regarding System Integrator or to change the Integrator. “I will ask the CEO to verify the system and take necessary steps to update it,” he said.

articles.title: Container movement to resume at Vallarpadam on November 23 as truck drivers end scanner boycott over health risks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The strike had left over 1,800 containers, including refrigerated ones carrying perishable goods, piled up at the terminal, triggering serious concerns among the export-import community and merchants

Container movement at the Vallarpadam International Container Transhipment Terminal (ICTT) will resume on Monday (November 23, 2026) after being disrupted for two weeks due to a non-cooperation strike launched by truck drivers.

The protestors on Sunday (November 22) called off the indefinite scanner boycott they had launched on November 9 and the token strike scheduled for Monday (November 23). The decision to call off the protest was taken following talks held with authorities on Saturday (November 21) night.

The container truck drivers at ICTT had been on the strike against the Customs department’s decision to scan all import containers arriving at the Kochi port in accordance with a Central government directive. The drivers boycotted the work alleging that the radiation from the scanning process could cause health problems for them.

The strike had left over 1,800 containers, including refrigerated ones carrying perishable goods, piled up at the terminal, triggering serious concerns among the export-import community and merchants.

The Trade Union Coordination Committee (TUCC), representing various unions, decided to resume work after authorities agreed to hear the workers’ complaints and put in place measures to address their concerns.

“Though similar concerns had been raised earlier, investigations conducted by the District Medical Officer and an advocate commissioner had found no reason for alarm. However, workers began the non-cooperation agitation after the scanning requirement was increased to 100% of containers, from the earlier rate of 20% to 80%. The meeting decided to examine whether such health risks existed and explore possible solutions,” an official release from the government said.

A demonstration of the scanning process will be held at the scanning site on Monday (November 23) for visitors as part of the decisions taken at Saturday’s (November 21) meeting. The measure is aimed at establishing that scanning will be carried out only after the truck driver moves at least 50 cm away from the cabin and that no radioactive activity reaches the driver’s cabin during the process, according to officials.

A medical team will also conduct a detailed examination of the health conditions of around 3,000 workers who have been employed at the port since it began operations in 2018. The team will submit its report within three months.

The State government will ask the Central government, Customs and the port authorities to conduct a detailed study and submit a report on possible arrangements, including the installation of conveyor belts, to prevent radiation exposure. The TUCC said though it was not fully satisfied with the decision to call off the scanner boycott, it decided to withdraw the agitation in view of the decisions and assurances given at the meeting.

Ernakulam MP Hibi Eden, MLAs Mohammed Shiyas, Tony Chammany and T.J. Vinod, District Collector G. Priyanka, the District Police Chief (Kochi city), Customs Commissioner, DP World officials and trade union leaders took part in the talks.

articles.title: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hailing from Parbhani in Maharashtra's Marathwada region, Mr. Wadkute was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April this year

BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute, who was elected to the Upper House earlier this year, died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi, family sources said on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Mr. Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS in the national capital on November 20 after complaining of a cough. He suffered a heart attack around 6 p.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026) and died during treatment around 11.45 p.m., they said.

Hailing from Parbhani in Maharashtra 's Marathwada region, Mr. Wadkute was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April this year and had previously served as a member of the State Legislative Council from June 2014 to October 2019.

Condoling the demise of the senior leader, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said his death was the loss of a simple and dedicated personality in politics who was deeply concerned about grassroots welfare.
Mr. Fadnavis noted that Mr. Wadkute had held several organisational responsibilities in the BJP in Hingoli district and worked extensively for the Dhangar community.
He also served as chairman of the Sheep and Goat Development Corporation and made his mark in the cooperative sector, the Chief Minister added.

President Droupadi Murmu mourned the demise Mr. Wadkute and remembered him for making valuable contributions to the development of Maharashtra and the nation. “Deeply saddened by the demise of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute Ji. He was dedicated to the cause of public welfare and made valuable contributions to the development of Maharashtra and the nation. My heartfelt condolences to his family members, admirers and well-wishers,” the President said in a post on X.

Also condoling Mr. Wadkute’s death, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that he will be remembered for his contribution to society and service to the poor and downtrodden. “Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden,” Mr. Modi said in a post on ‘X’.
The Prime Minister said equally noteworthy were Mr. Wadkute’s efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra.

Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute Ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden. Equally noteworthy were his efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. My thoughts are with his family and admirers. Om Shanti. राज्यसभा खासदार श्री रामराव वडकुते जी यांच्या निधनाचे वृत्त ऐकून अतिशय दुःख झाले. समाजसेवेतील त्यांचे योगदान तसेच गरीब आणि वंचित घटकांच्या सेवेसाठी त्यांनी दिलेले प्राधान्य यासाठी त्यांचे सदैव स्मरण केले जाईल. महाराष्ट्रात भाजप पक्ष संघटना बळकट करण्यासाठी त्यांनी केलेले प्रयत्नही तितकेच उल्लेखनीय होते. या दुःखद प्रसंगी त्यांच्या कुटुंबीयांच्या आणि चाहत्यांच्या दुःखात मी सहभागी आहे. ओम शांती.
Vice-President and Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan expressed grief over Mr. Wadkute's passing, saying his contributions to public life and service to the people will always be remembered.

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said, "The passing of Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute ji is deeply saddening. In this hour of grief, my heartfelt condolences are with the bereaved family. May the departed soul rest in peace and may the family find the strength to bear this immense loss."

At least four people were killed ​and 30 injured in ‌a fire at a power ​station in southern Iraq ⁠on Saturday (November 21, 2026), with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence ‌teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north of Basra ‌under ⁠control after firefighters responded ⁠to the incident, Iraq’s state news agency, INA , reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring ​houses and ‌forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.
The Hartha station ‌has an installed generating ​capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at ⁠around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.
There was no ‌immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq’s electricity infrastructure has long struggled ‌with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance ​, and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during ⁠the extremely hot summer months. Fires ⁠and technical failures at substations and power facilities have ‌previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

articles.title: South Korea Education Minister resigns amid AI cheating scandal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score
South Korea's Education Minister resigned on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted ahead of the country's key college entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial college entrance exam known as the Suneung.
The annual nine-hour Suneung is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures — including blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons but Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam.

"The exam concluded without any major incidents... However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance," Mr. Choi wrote on X.
"Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation," he added.
President Lee Jae Myung has accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday (November 16, 2026) whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied: "Due to my age, I am not confident I could."
Mr. Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, nearly half of which were detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones that test takers had failed to hand over.

articles.title: North Korea delays international marathon until October: tour agency

fullParagraphs: It was held last year for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, but this year's race, scheduled for April, was cancelled with no reason given

North Korea has postponed its annual international marathon, which gives runners from around the world a rare glimpse of the secretive state's capital city, by six months until next October, a tour agency has said.

The race, which has historically seen hundreds of local and foreign athletes pound the streets of Pyongyang before finishing in front of thousands of fans at Kim Il Sung Stadium, is the diplomatically isolated state's largest international sporting event.
It was held last year for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, but this year's race, scheduled for April, was cancelled with no reason given.
The next edition, initially slated for April 2027, will now take place in October, Beijing-based Koryo Tours, which describes itself as the marathon's exclusive partner, said.

The company "has been informed by our partners in the Pyongyang International Marathon Committee that the date for the 2027 marathon is being changed", it said on its website on Saturday (November 22, 2026).
"It will not take place in April 2027. Instead, it is almost certain that the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon will happen in October 2027," it added.
"We hope to have a fully confirmed date in good time," it said, without giving a reason for the change.
Last year's race, the first in six years, drew about 200 foreign runners who competed alongside more than 200 North Koreans. Local athletes won both the men's and women's events.
The number of foreign participants was significantly lower than 2019, when about 950 foreigners competed.
But the North cancelled this year's race, with Koryo Tours announcing in March that the decision had been confirmed by the country's athletics association.

articles.title: Immigration officers make arrest at Seattle airport in ‘distressing’ scene, delaying flight
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would "engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred"

Masked immigration officers detained at least one person on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding, causing what the airline called a "distressing" scene for passengers and employees and delaying the Los Angeles-bound flight.

Video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday (November 22, 2026) as a woman screams that her daughter is being taken and she has a work permit.
Online flight data showed that Alaska flight 1306, which had been scheduled to depart at 8:10 a.m., was delayed.
Alaska Airlines said Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

"We are concerned by this morning's law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306," the airline said. "We recognise how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests."
It added that the airline is committed to "treating every guest with dignity and respect".
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.
The arresting officers wore unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The video showed them struggling with someone on the ground as passengers surrounded by rolling suitcases looked on.
ICE has stepped up arrests at airports since the summer, especially targeting people who overstayed visas in the past.

Alaska Airlines said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and also that it has raised concerns "directly with the appropriate authorities".

The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would "engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred".
Washington Gov Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, called the incident "just the latest example of ICE's deeply un-American tactics".

articles.title: COP31: Turkiye's final draft doesn't mention the words ‘fossil fuels’ that cause global warming
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: COP31 President Murat Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary

The newest and possibly final proposed agreement to come out of United Nations climate talks doesn't contain the words fossil fuels , the chief cause of global warming, or specifically call for transitioning away from the coal, oil and gas that spew carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

The draft from Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum, president of the two-week conference in Antalya, Turkiye, called COP31, was released in the wee hours of Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning. Mr. Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary.

There must be near-unanimous consensus for approval and several countries earlier in negotiations made vociferous objections to omitting a call to phase out fossil fuels. But the proposal does put a specific goal on a technology, supported by the oil industry, of capturing carbon pollution and storing it.

Because the text went to negotiators and the public after 3 a.m., countries and activists did not immediately respond to the newest version. The conference was scheduled to end Friday (November 20, 2026) and is now in double overtime . Organisers worry that as negotiators depart there may not be a voting quorum of 2/3 of the delegates, which would prevent passage of the draft.

Earlier in the week, Panama vowed to formally object to a final agreement that didn't put a cap on oil production, acknowledge failing goals to limit warming and beef up finance for nations to adapt to warming's harms. Panama Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro said the talks were being held hostage by a “petroleum mafia” and need to be reformed.

Fossil fuels also went unmentioned in final decisions for more than 25 years, mostly because of objections by Saudi Arabia, said Alden Meyer, a longtime analyst with the European think-tank E3G. He added, however, that the world agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” in Dubai in 2023.
COP31 opens as climate and geopolitical pressures mount
COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
“It would be a real setback if we come out of here with no signal that we were serious about what we agreed to do three years ago,” Mr. Meyer said.

The proposed final agreement makes a reference to the Dubai agreement in the first line, saying it is “recalling the United Arab Emirates Consensus in its entirety,” but the words “fossil,” “oil” or “coal” or “phase out” do not appear anywhere in the 10-page text.

The agreement also calls for countries to increase the share of total final energy consumption, which includes switching transportation such as cars, trucks and planes to electricity from gas, to 35% from about 21% now by 2035. This has been Turkiye's signature effort.

Climate activists also have sought a provision stating the electricity should only come from renewable energy, such as wind and solar, arguing that allowing electricity powered by fossil fuel in the goal defeats the purpose of lowering emissions.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 60 discusses healthcare spending, antimicrobial resistance and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The episode discuss trends in healthcare expenditure in India, concerns over the regulation of fertility services, the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance, and the impact of environmental and social conditions on public health

The 60th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu looks at key developments in public including healthcare financing, reproductive health, antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, environmental exposures and diabetes care.

Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the latest National Health Accounts estimates for 2023–24, which show a substantial increase in government health expenditure and a decline in the share of household out-of-pocket spending nationally. The episode also examines the contrasting trends in Keralam, where household healthcare expenditure has increased and the share of government spending has declined.

The episode looks at the drug regulator’s direction to pharmaceutical companies to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs and the potential implications for treatment costs. It also examines concerns over an illegal human egg collection racket in Telangana, including questions about informed consent, women’s safety and the regulation of assisted reproductive technology centres. Developments in Karnataka’s proposed mid-life women’s health programme and mandatory gynaecological check-ups for girls are also discussed.

Marking World AMR Awareness Week, the episode explores the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and the need for appropriate antibiotic use, timely diagnosis, infection prevention and surveillance. It also discusses phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to target bacterial infections, and its potential role in addressing infections that do not respond to conventional antibiotics.

The discussion also examines tuberculosis through the lens of social and economic vulnerability, highlighting the importance of nutrition, housing and social support alongside diagnosis and treatment. It looks at the latest figures on domestic funding for India’s TB response, which now accounts for 86% of total spending, even as external funding declines.

The discussion also examines the health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women and newborns. A survey of healthcare professionals across five countries found that 98% of Indian clinicians surveyed had treated pregnant women and newborns whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat.

The episode also looks into how fear of diagnosis may discourage people from screening and discusses a Chennai initiative that uses dietary counselling by staff nurses to improve blood sugar control and support long-term diabetes management.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens

From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures.

That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says.

Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area.

Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals.

From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001

The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026).

A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

articles.title: T.N. to set up Statewide online registry of voluntary donors with rare blood groups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC).
In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry.
The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups.
The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent.

The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry.

The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed.

At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations.

In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator. Each club will be linked to a nearby licensed blood centre, and regular voluntary blood donation camps should be organised.

The order noted that voluntary blood donation is an essential component of safe and adequate blood supply. Sustaining an adequate blood supply requires continuous mobilisation of voluntary non-remunerated blood donors, particularly among the youth and student population.

RRCs have an established a network of student members, faculty coordinators and institutional support. The RRCs can provide an effective platform for introducing a dedicated Blood Donor Club in colleges without creating a new institutional mechanism, it said.
Both these initiatives were among the announcements made by the Health Minister in the Assembly early this year.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme
Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status.

According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status.
The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030.

The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment.

According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres.
The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment.
Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October.

The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 22 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme

Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status.

According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status.

The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030.

The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment.

According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres.

The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment.

Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October.

The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets.

Mr. Satya Kumar said priority was to ensure timely diagnosis, continuous treatment and quality healthcare without discrimination for everyone living with HIV.

APSACS Project Director Smaran Raj said the organisation was committed to bringing three more districts to ‘Surakshit’ status in the week.

articles.title: Healthcare AI: hospitals lack capacity to measure real-world patient outcomes, warns French expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Emmanuel Bacry warns that laboratory accuracy scores do not establish real-world clinical benefits; says healthcare AI trained largely on Western data may not work elsewhere

Hospitals worldwide are ill-equipped to assess whether artificial intelligence (AI) systems deployed in their facilities actually improve patient outcomes, raising questions about the clinical and economic value of healthcare AI, Emmanuel Bacry, Scientific Director of France’s Health Data Hub, said at the Bengaluru Tech Summit.

“There are maybe six or seven hospitals in the whole world today that are able to evaluate medical devices deployed in their system,” Mr. Bacry said. Hospitals struggle to access and integrate patient information to track outcomes after discharge, including recovery rates and mortality, making it difficult to establish the actual impact of AI-based medical technologies.
“In hospitals, we don’t know how to compute that,” he said, referring to the return on investment of such technologies. “So imagine now, if they adopt AI.”

Mr. Bacry cited an alert system based on rules-based AI, or an expert system, designed to warn intensive care unit (ICU) staff about severe kidney failure. Despite functioning effectively, the system was associated with a doubling of deaths in two of the six US hospitals where it was deployed in 2022, he said. He did not identify the study.

While researchers had offered hypotheses, the precise cause remained unknown. Mr. Bacry suggested that the absence of a tested response protocol among hospital personnel could have contributed to the outcome.

“We just replaced the alert done by a human with the alert done by the medical device. And that changes the whole thing,” he said, underlining the importance of integrating AI into clinical workflows rather than treating it as a standalone technology.

He also cautioned against evaluating diagnostic AI tools solely through laboratory accuracy scores or comparisons with doctors. A system achieving 95% accuracy against a doctor’s 90% might not necessarily perform better in clinical settings. “When you deploy in real life, you can forget about these scores,” he said.

Mr. Bacry flagged another concern: AI systems can identify patterns that even their developers cannot explain. Citing research, he said one model predicted ethnicity from chest X-rays with approximately 85% accuracy, while another inferred sex from eye images with 95% accuracy.
Such hidden correlations could influence medical decisions without clinicians understanding the underlying basis, potentially introducing unintended bias into diagnosis and treatment.

In a separate interaction with The Hindu, Mr. Bacry warned that healthcare AI development was heavily skewed towards Western populations. By his estimate, nearly 70% of global healthcare AI training data came from male, white and Western populations.
“We are developing an Occidental AI and even narrow types of Occidental AI,” he said.

He advocated smaller, locally tailored AI models trained on representative population data, arguing that deploying large, general-purpose models without adaptation could have disastrous consequences, particularly in developing countries.

articles.title: i-ALERT system leads to savings, lesser emissions for RTC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month

The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) announced that they are the first State Road Transport Corporation in India to introduce the i-ALERT system in its BS-VI buses and indicated its implementation has saved the organisation approximately ₹36 crore in diesel costs.

According to the state-run road transport undertaking, the i-ALERT tool monitors and assesses driving patterns. It keeps tabs on gear selection, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and braking practices, thus assisting drivers to adopt safer and more fuel-efficient driving methods.

The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month. The corporation estimates its monthly savings at ₹2 crore.

The reduction in fuel consumption has also cut carbon emissions. With every litre of diesel estimated to generate 2.56 kg of carbon emissions, the initiative has helped reduce CO2 emissions by 16.90 metric tonnes a day, 507.11 tonnes a month and 6,169.84 tons annually, the TGSRTC stated.

The system also enables the corporation to assess individual driver performance after every duty and provide feedback and grades. Drivers are monitored for adherence to the prescribed Green Band RPM range, efficient use of economy gears, reduction in engine idling, avoidance of over speeding and appropriate braking practices.

TGSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Anil Kumar congratulated the engineering department for adopting the technology. He urged other departments to adopt modern technology to further improve the corporation’s services.
APSRTC and KSRTC have approached senior TGSRTC officials seeking information on the performance of the i-ALERT system, the corporation said.

articles.title: U.P. Police mistakenly give guard of honour to Owaisi in Saharanpur, probe ordered
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police team had reached the circuit house in the morning to prepare for a Supreme Court judge's arrival; however, the judge had not reached the premises when Asaduddin Owaisi arrived there, and the personnel reportedly got confused

Police personnel in Saharanpur on Saturday (November 21, 2026) mistakenly gave a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi at the circuit house, apparently mistaking him for a Supreme Court judge who was scheduled to visit the premises, prompting an inquiry into the incident.

The police team had reached the circuit house in the morning to prepare for the judge's arrival. However, the judge had not reached the premises when Mr. Owaisi arrived, and the personnel reportedly got confused and accorded him the ceremonial salute.
Mr. Owaisi's visit to the circuit house was apparently not part of his original programme, and he arrived there unexpectedly, according to local inputs.

Mr. Owaisi was in the district, accompanied by Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) chief Chandrashekhar Aazad. The two leaders were in Saharanpur to hold a joint press conference ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
Mr. Owaisi stood and accepted the salute as the police personnel accorded him the guard of honour.
The two leaders had recently announced the formation of the Samajik Parivartan Morcha (SPM), a joint political front to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
In a statement, Saharanpur Police said the senior superintendent of police has directed the superintendent of police (Rural) to investigate the incident.
"Action as per rules will be ensured on the basis of facts and evidence obtained after the inquiry," the police said.
The incident has raised questions over the apparent lapse in identifying the person for whom the ceremonial honour was being arranged.
Guard of honour is a ceremonial military or police salute in which personnel stand in formation to honour designated dignitaries on official or formal occasions.

fullParagraphs: Apart from the usual distribution of organisational berths to poll-going States, caste groups, and other demographics of sex and age, the new BJP team reflects the party’s attempts at a reset. Nistula Hebbar reports on how three terms in power have brought both the pieties of the past and anxieties of the future into focus

Prime Minister Narendra Modi walked into a meeting of the newly appointed Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national office-bearers on August 22. The 64 office-bearers present assumed he would address them on how they should approach their assignments. Instead, he spent the next four-and-a-quarter hours individually querying them on their past organisational work.

The exchange was unhurried, with PM Modi at one point telling the audience that he too was once like them, a national office-bearer of the party during the late Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure as Prime Minister (1999-2004), say some of the new office-bearers.

The identification was interpreted in some quarters as a pep talk to the new team of how far organisational service can take you in the BJP, but for others it pointed to a unifying characteristic in a list of names that otherwise lacked a meta narrative, and instead, in a piecemeal fashion exhibited the political anxieties of the BJP.

This privileging of organisational experience by the Prime Minister was the highlight of the new team. The BJP, now in its third term in power and seeking a fourth in 2029, is, with this new team, attempting a reset amid various political anxieties.

Journalist Shekhar Iyer, who has tracked the BJP for decades, says, “The new team marks a big shift in the party top brass’ approach to the challenges ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha poll. Increasingly, the BJP is signalling to itself that, henceforth, the chosen men and women will represent less of their individual personality and more of their abilities and capabilities for the tasks to be accomplished.”

articles.title: BJP appoints Yuzvendra Chahal as special invitee to OBC Morcha executive committee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on November 21, 2026, announced fresh appointments of national office-bearers, national executive members, and department heads for its OBC Morcha with immediate effect
Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has been appointed as a Special Invitee to the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) National Other Backwards Classes (OBC) Morcha executive committee.

BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday (November 21, 2026) announced fresh appointments of national office-bearers, national executive members, and department heads for its OBC Morcha with immediate effect.

According to the official communication issued by the party’s central office, the list includes seven national vice presidents, three national general secretaries, and seven national secretaries representing various states across the country.

The seven newly appointed national vice presidents of the BJP OBC Morcha are Jogen Mohan (Assam), Mamata Mohanta (Odisha), Sangam Lal Gupta (Uttar Pradesh), Babanrao Ravji Choudhary (Maharashtra), Sat Prakash Rana (Delhi), Arjun Sahani (Bihar), and Sangeeta Balwant Bind (Uttar Pradesh). Gajendra Yadav (Delhi), Pramod Madhwaraj (Karnataka), and Lalit Chandrakar (Chhattisgarh) have been named as national general secretaries.

The party also appointed seven national secretaries: Dashrathji Thakor (Gujarat), T Varatharajan (Tamil Nadu), Sanjeev Kumar alias Bablu Bhagat (Jharkhand), Sarita Jangid (Haryana), Kadaganchi Ramesh (Telangana), Vaibhav Panwar (Madhya Pradesh), and Bhim Kumar Sahu (Bihar). Under the organisational appointments, Radheshyam Yadav from Uttar Pradesh has been given charge as the national treasurer. Sanjay Kumar Gurjar and Dr Arun Yadav (both from Delhi) have been appointed as national office secretary and co-office secretary, respectively.

Ajay Gupta from Bihar has been named the media coordinator for the Morcha. For digital communication, Parikshit Dagar (Delhi) has been appointed social media coordinator, with Pradeep Mahaur Soni (Madhya Pradesh) named co-coordinator.
Prof. Pankaj Choudhary (Delhi) will head the policy and research wing as coordinator, assisted by co-coordinators Ashutosh Behera (Odisha) and Rahul Yadav (Uttar Pradesh).

The party also notified the initial names of the national executive committee members, including Sanjeev Rangaiya (Andaman & Nicobar), Srinivas Rao Kantubukta (Andhra Pradesh), Rajiv Ranjan alias Vishal Yadav (Bihar), and Sanjeev Verma (Chandigarh).

articles.title: Palaniswami criticises TVK-led government over SC dismissal of TN’s Cauvery pleas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a social media post, Palaniswami claimed the CM was not aware of the Supreme Court’s decision

AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Sunday (November 22, 2026) criticised the Tamil Nadu government, led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, after the Supreme Court dismissed two applications filed by the State in connection with the Cauvery water dispute.
In a social media post, Mr. Palaniswami claimed the CM was not aware of the Supreme Court’s decision. .

“You (Mr Vijay) will not convene an all-party meeting over the Cauvery dispute. You will not engage with the Congress leadership on the issue or pursue the legal battle effectively. And you will pose for photographs without condemning Karnataka CM, who has been speaking against Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Palaniswami said.

The AIADMK leader warned the inadequate release of Cauvery water by Karnataka along with the “TVK-led alliance government’s failure” to secure Tamil Nadu’s rightful share, could adversely affect the samba cultivation season.

Questioning the Chief Minister’s priorities, Mr. Palaniswami charged that the CM had failed to raise the concerns of Tamil Nadu’s farmers during his recent meeting with Congress leader Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi. [Mr Vijay had gone to attend a function to mark the launch of Ms Gandhi’s memoirs.]

Mr. Vijay was playing with the rights linked with the lifeline of Tamil Nadu and the lives of the farmers in the State, Mr. Palaniswami said. Recalling the AIADMK’s efforts under former CMs M.G. Ramachandran, Jayalalithaa and himself, Mr. Palaniswami contended the party had fought to secure the State’s Cauvery rights over the Cauvery issue.

articles.title: Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘We were weak, but we are not weak now. We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party,’ says Rajendra Pal Gautam

The Congress is hopeful of forging an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election but wants a “respectable” seat-sharing arrangement, All India Congress Committee in-charge for the State Rajendra Pal Gautam has said.

Mr. Gautam, in an interview with The Hindu , said the two parties are expected to hold formal seat-sharing discussions this week and asserted that the Congress would make the alleged “ chanda chori ” (theft of temple donations) a major campaign issue.

Though he did not disclose the exact date, the first meeting is likely to be held on Monday afternoon. Senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K.C. Venugopal, and Mr. Gautam, are expected to participate.

Commenting on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s recent statement that the Congress had sought 181 seats, Mr. Gautam said, “I am not going to reveal which seats, but we have given them a list. We will try to convince them, and I am sure they will try to convince us. The outcome depends on these talks.”
Asked whether the Congress would settle for an alliance at any cost, Mr. Gautam said: “It is not like that at all. The understanding will be a respectable one.”

Countering suggestions that the Congress lacked the organisational strength to bargain for a substantial share of seats, Mr. Gautam pointed out that while the SP won 37 seats and the Congress six in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP’s alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls had not yielded similar results.
“We were weak, but we are not weak now,” he said, adding, “We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party.”

On whether the Congress was attempting social engineering to regain the support of the Brahmin, Dalit, and Muslim communities that had once formed its core constituency, he claimed that every section of society is now gravitating toward the party. “Every section is feeling cheated, whether Brahmins, Dalits, OBCs, or Muslims,” he said.

The party also intends to highlight the alleged chadhava-chori (theft of offerings and donations) at Lord Ram’s temple in Ayodhya. The campaign, scheduled to begin in the first week of December, will take the issue to villages, chaupals, and gram panchayats.

“ Chadhava-chori, chanda-chori will be one of our main issues in the election. The BJP came to power using faith and then betrayed the people. In every press conference and public meeting, we will raise it,” he said.

Mr. Gautam also listed key campaign issues including the alleged closure of 27,000 government schools, reduced scholarships, rising education costs, discrimination in recruitment, failure to fill vacancies reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, alleged atrocities against Dalits and OBCs, distress among farmers, questionable police encounters, and the demolition of houses using bulldozers.

On the emergence of a new political front involving AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi and Dalit leader Chandrashekhar Azad, Mr. Gautam said: “Voters in U.P. are intelligent enough to understand who this is intended to benefit,” hinting that the move would help the ruling BJP by splitting Opposition votes.

articles.title: Plan approach paper eyes leveraging heft of Keralam’s economy for 15th Five-Year Plan period
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The UDF government and the Planning Board have visualised a ‘partnership economy’ for building the economy up from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore by 2031-32

In targeting a 7% growth in real terms during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2027-2032), the UDF government is hoping to leverage the heft of Keralam’s economy, which, according to the State Planning Board’s approach paper to the 15th Plan, “contains far more capital than its government commands.”

Real growth of 7% a year for five years (2027-2032) at the incremental capital-output ratio (the measure of how much investment is needed to generate a unit of economic growth) of around 4, implies investment of ₹4.5 lakh crore a year, according to the approach paper. The 2026-27 Revised Budget on the other hand estimates a capital expenditure of only ₹22,566 crore. “About ₹19 in ₹20 of the investment Keralam needs will therefore come from outside the State Budget,” the paper, published last week, notes.

On money outside the Budget, the approach paper has this to say: “Bank deposits stand at ₹10,84,241 crore and advances at ₹7,81,043 crore, a credit-deposit ratio of 72.04%. Non-resident deposits are ₹2,86,063 crore. Primary agricultural credit societies hold nearly ₹1.3 lakh crore, about 70% of all such deposits in the country. Remittances were ₹2,16,893 crore in 2023. Bank lending depends on the availability of bankable projects, so the gap between deposits and advances measures the shortage of bankable projects in the State more than any shortage of savings. If credit to the Plan’s engines rose by the equivalent of 8% points of deposits, about ₹87,000 crore more would be at work in Keralam, nearly four times the annual capital budget.”
The task of planning will therefore be to direct that capital to productive use within the State, according to the paper.
The UDF government and the Planning Board have visualised a ‘partnership economy’ for building the economy up from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore by 2031-32.

The approach paper to the 14th Five-Year Plan had noted that mobilising resources for the Plan period (2022-2027) would be a “challenging task.” The scenario has not changed much. The White Paper on Keralam’s fiscal health laid in the Legislative Assembly in June this year had observed that “behind Keralam’s social achievements lies a fiscal structure that is under serious and growing strain.”

The approach paper for the 15th Plan draws a grim picture of present-day Keralam. The State is a “picture of slow growth, low investment, large youth unemployment and an ageing population. The State’s fiscal space is rather limited, and its revenue base is weak. There is no hope of large Union transfers.”

articles.title: CJP plans to take ‘Cockroach Club’ across India, shifts youth movement beyond street protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Launched in Pune with over 300 participants, the initiative will combine political debates, lectures, film screenings, comedy and cultural performances as the party seeks to channelise youth energy into shaping India’s future

Moving beyond street mobilisation, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is looking to build a nationwide network of cultural and discussion spaces with its newly launched ‘Cockroach Club’. The party wants the initiative to reach every part of the country, including remote villages, as it seeks to give young people a platform to debate public issues, exchange ideas and envision the future they want for India, its co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka said during an interaction with The Hindu.

The club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21 and brought together more than 300 people for an event lasting around three hours. The programme featured comedy, satire and conversations on Mahatma Gandhi, while participants discussed local issues concerning Maharashtra. Performances addressing larger issues facing the country were also part of the event.

“This is a platform where we can all come together and articulate the future we want for ourselves and answer some difficult questions we want to address. The idea of Cockroach Clubs is to have a space where people can come, talk, brainstorm, collaborate and envision what they want our country to be,” Mr. Ranka said.

Explaining why Pune was chosen for the first gathering, he said the party had a large support base in Maharashtra, while Delhi was also an important centre for the organisation and would soon feature in its plans.
“The idea is for the Cockroach Club to go to every corner of the country. This is a truly national movement and everything has to come together,” he added.

CJP co-convenor Saurav Das said the club was envisioned as a “physical space for the younger generation” to come together, exchange ideas, question, learn and grow. It would host lectures and discussions on the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, B.R. Ambedkar and other thinkers, besides film screenings, live performances and stand-up comedy.
The space would also offer young people a quiet corner to read, study, and prepare for examinations, while allowing them to unwind and interact, he said.

“This was just a trailer. As we go ahead, we will know what can be bettered. We will use this platform to discuss how to take this movement forward, how to get more and more people to join, and channelise the energy of the youth in a structured manner to bring a change in the country,” Mr. Das said.

He said the club would encourage young people to think for themselves rather than have opinions handed down to them or ideologies imposed on them. “We the young will develop our Idea of India at the Cockroach Club,” he said.
Over 300 people gathered at the Gandhi Bhavan, Kothrud in Pune for Cockroach Club’s first gathering, titled ‘Legacy of Bapu’, was held in Pune on November 21. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

The first event was not ticketed, Mr. Ranka said. The local Pune team initially pooled money to organise the event, followed by local fundraising. A collection was also made at the venue, where participants contributed to their capacity.
The party is yet to decide how it will fund the initiative as it expands. It could consider introducing tickets for future events or continue with the local fundraising model, he said.

articles.title: JKSSB exam cheating racket: Six more arrested; six government employees among accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police said the question paper was allegedly taken out of the examination centre, photographed and circulated among selected candidates through Telegram

Six more persons were arrested in the ongoing investigation into the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted recently by Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board, taking the total arrests to 20, with police clarifying that the malpractice was confined to a specific examination centre and did not involve a paper leak.

The accused include six government employees, among them the alleged mastermind. Police said the question paper was allegedly taken out of the examination centre, photographed and circulated among selected candidates through Telegram.
14 arrested as J&K Police bust exam cheating racket; mobiles, wireless sets seized

The investigation has also revealed financial transactions of ₹1.80 lakh, of which ₹1.40 lakh has been recovered, while the accused had allegedly negotiated payments of ₹10–12 lakh from candidates in exchange for helping them clear the examination, Jammu Senior Superintendent of Police Joginder Singh said at a press conference in Jammu.

On November 15, police in Jammu arrested 14 suspects ahead of the FAA exam, “uncovering” a network that planned to transmit answers to select candidates inside the exam centres through electronic communication devices.
Several wireless radio sets were seized in the intelligence-based operation, three FIRs were lodged, and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the alleged conspiracy.

Disclosing details of the investigation, the SSP said the probe had led to the identification and arrest of the alleged main kingpin, whose interrogation brought to light a wider network involving candidates, government employees and other intermediaries.

"Of the 20 persons arrested so far, six are government employees. Their details have been shared with the respective departments for departmental action. At the same time, criminal proceedings are also being pursued based on their alleged roles," he said, clarifying that none of the arrested persons belonged to the JKSSB.
According to the investigation, Mr. Singh said the alleged mastermind had initially planned to facilitate cheating for two persons — a close relative and a friend.

However, another accused involved in the operation allegedly created a separate network and contacted 20 to 22 additional candidates. He reportedly collected their original documents and obtained blank cheques from four to five candidates, with an understanding that payments would be made after they successfully cleared the examination.

Police said the question paper was accessed with the alleged assistance of an employee posted at the examination centre. After the examination began, papers placed on the desks of absent candidates were collected and taken to a designated room. “The employee allegedly removed one of the papers and handed it to another person, as he could not leave the examination centre,” the SSP said.

He said the second person then passed it on to an accused waiting outside, who allegedly took it to his car, photographed it and returned it for deposit at the centre. The photographs were subsequently circulated through a Telegram group to facilitate cheating by selected candidates.

articles.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue ‘leaves options open’ for Pakistan SCO meets next year, say sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As the government faces criticism over “inconsistency” in the invitation to Pakistan, officials say the invite can be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility”

The visit of Pakistan Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Musadik Malik, to India, the first by any senior Pakistani official since 2023, was a “Shanghai Cooperation Organisation” (SCO) initiative, not an Indian one alone, said officials as the government came under criticism from the Opposition.

However, former Indian diplomats who served in Pakistan said the visit and the invitation to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi and the SCO Summit to be held in Pakistan next year could be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility” and providing a multilateral platform for the region, when bilateral moves, and the SAARC Summit are not taking place.

Ministry of External Affairs officials have stressed that there were no “bilateral” or one-to-one meetings during the three-day event hosted at Delhi’s iconic Purana Kila (Old Fort) monument. Ministers from six countries – Pakistan, Tajikistan, Nepal, Azerbaijan, Iran, and the Kyrgyz Republic – and Deputy Ministers from eight other countries participated in the forum.

Government officials pointed out that the event allows India a chance to highlight its cultural prowess and strong roots and furthers India’s common links with other members of the SCO, which also see themselves as “civilizational” states. It is also significant that India has carved out a space for itself in the year when Pakistan is the Chair of the SCO, they said, and is leading a shift in the grouping’s more security-oriented and land-locked focus to a more South Asian, oceanic and people-to-people linked focus.

They suggested that such meetings could also pave the way for next year, when External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will all be invited to Pakistan for SCO meetings chaired by Pakistan, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be invited to the Heads of Council meeting to be held in the third quarter of 2027. Government officials said it was too early to speak about participation in these meetings in Pakistan yet, but that a decision closer to the dates would only be possible if options were kept open at present, and SCO events in the run-up to the Summit are kept away from the “negativity” of bilateral relations.

“The meeting was in an SCO context so it would be inappropriate to read into it any bilateral content, leave alone a breakthrough,” said former Indian High Commissioner to Islamabad TCA Raghavan (2013-2015). He added, however, that “given the precarious and fraught state of India- Pakistan relations, an episode of common civility and normalcy is a plus and, even without intending to, creates possibilities.”

Former High Commissioner to Islamabad Ajay Bisaria (2017-2019), who was the last to serve in Pakistan before both sides downgraded ties in 2019, said that Mr. Malik’s visit to India represented “more than a formality but less than a thaw” and demonstrated how such multilateral events allow India and Pakistan to “tolerate each other’s presence, even when they won’t engage directly”. When asked about India’s attendance at SCO events in Pakistan next year, Mr. Bisaria said that the “ball is in Pakistan’s court” to “dial down both terrorism and rhetoric” if it hopes for Indian leaders to travel there. Significantly, he said such an event could be an opportunity to revive the SAARC process as well, that has been suspended for a decade.

On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making the point that while “empires had redrawn maps”, such dialogues had “transformed and enriched global thought”. Mr. Modi had proposed the Dialogue at the SCO Summit in Tianjin in 2025, and the proposal was adopted at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in October 2026, with the declaration announcing that it would be held in Delhi this month.

The criticism was particularly sharp over images this weekend of Mr. Modi and the Pakistani Minister seated in the first row, as well as of Culture Minister and host Gajendra Singh Shekhawat holding a conversation with Mr. Malik at a lunch table.

“This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, underlining at briefings held in the past week that the government has not changed its position on other outstanding bilateral issues with Pakistan including over the Pahalgam terror attack, and the suspension of the Indus Water Treaty.
