🏛️ National & Polity 📅 22 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

SCO Civilisational Dialogue ‘leaves options open’ for Pakistan SCO meets next year, say sources

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

As the government faces criticism over “inconsistency” in the invitation to Pakistan, officials say the invite can be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility”

The visit of Pakistan Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Musadik Malik, to India, the first by any senior Pakistani official since 2023, was a “Shanghai Cooperation Organisation” (SCO) initiative, not an Indian one alone, said officials as the government came under criticism from the Opposition.

However, former Indian diplomats who served in Pakistan said the visit and the invitation to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi and the SCO Summit to be held in Pakistan next year could be seen as building a window of opportunity for “common civility” and providing a multilateral platform for the region, when bilateral moves, and the SAARC Summit are not taking place.

Ministry of External Affairs officials have stressed that there were no “bilateral” or one-to-one meetings during the three-day event hosted at Delhi’s iconic Purana Kila (Old Fort) monument. Ministers from six countries – Pakistan, Tajikistan, Nepal, Azerbaijan, Iran, and the Kyrgyz Republic – and Deputy Ministers from eight other countries participated in the forum.

Government officials pointed out that the event allows India a chance to highlight its cultural prowess and strong roots and furthers India’s common links with other members of the SCO, which also see themselves as “civilizational” states. It is also significant that India has carved out a space for itself in the year when Pakistan is the Chair of the SCO, they said, and is leading a shift in the grouping’s more security-oriented and land-locked focus to a more South Asian, oceanic and people-to-people linked focus.

They suggested that such meetings could also pave the way for next year, when External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will all be invited to Pakistan for SCO meetings chaired by Pakistan, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be invited to the Heads of Council meeting to be held in the third quarter of 2027. Government officials said it was too early to speak about participation in these meetings in Pakistan yet, but that a decision closer to the dates would only be possible if options were kept open at present, and SCO events in the run-up to the Summit are kept away from the “negativity” of bilateral relations.

“The meeting was in an SCO context so it would be inappropriate to read into it any bilateral content, leave alone a breakthrough,” said former Indian High Commissioner to Islamabad TCA Raghavan (2013-2015). He added, however, that “given the precarious and fraught state of India- Pakistan relations, an episode of common civility and normalcy is a plus and, even without intending to, creates possibilities.”

Former High Commissioner to Islamabad Ajay Bisaria (2017-2019), who was the last to serve in Pakistan before both sides downgraded ties in 2019, said that Mr. Malik’s visit to India represented “more than a formality but less than a thaw” and demonstrated how such multilateral events allow India and Pakistan to “tolerate each other’s presence, even when they won’t engage directly”. When asked about India’s attendance at SCO events in Pakistan next year, Mr. Bisaria said that the “ball is in Pakistan’s court” to “dial down both terrorism and rhetoric” if it hopes for Indian leaders to travel there. Significantly, he said such an event could be an opportunity to revive the SAARC process as well, that has been suspended for a decade.

In 2024, Mr. Jaishankar had travelled to Islamabad to represent India at the SCO Heads of Government Summit.

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year.

European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year.

The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules.

Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive.

The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU.
Watch | India–EU Free Trade Agreement explained: Biggest trade deal in India’s history | India-New Zealand FTA comes into force; new visa categories for Indians, zero-duty access for exports
Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion).
The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missile in western region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Saudi Arabia's western region contains key energy infrastructure including the Yanbu terminal, a major facility for crude oil exports
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said on Sunday (November 22, 2026) it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast.
"Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the western region," coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post.

Saudi Arabia's western region contains key energy infrastructure including the Yanbu terminal, a major facility for crude oil exports, and the Jazan refinery in the far southwest of the country bordering Yemen.
Houthi fighters have attacked these major oil installations in recent weeks, alongside strikes on airports and military sites.
Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis, is the world's largest crude exporter.
Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in Saudi Arabia since September, including 23 in strikes on airports, according to the kingdom's authorities.

On Thursday (November 19), a tower housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh's financial district sustained damage on several floors in a Houthi attack, authorities said.
A skyscraper belonging to state oil giant Aramco was also damaged in a strike at the beginning of the month.

articles.title: Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

articles.title: Activists welcome KSPCB move to close down eight Koppal factories
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Farmers from affected villages and women from Koppal city join the celebrations and dance to the beats of traditional drums

Senior writer Allamaprabhu Bettadur and environmental activists dancing at the protest venue in Koppal to celebrate the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board decision to close down eight industrial units. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

Koppal District Bachao Andolan Samiti and the Parisara Hitarakshana Vedike, jointly campaigning against industrial pollution in the district, have welcomed the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) decision to close down eight sponge iron and steel units in the region.

The organisations welcomed the closure orders during their 385-days-old protest by distributing sweets and celebrating the development. Farmers from affected villages and women from Koppal city joined the celebrations and danced to the beats of traditional drums.

The eight units facing closure orders are Tanush Ispat Pvt. Ltd. Unit 1, Harekrishna Metallics Steel Pvt. Ltd. (Tanush Unit 2), P. Balasubbashetty and Sons (PBS Steel), Dhruvdesh Metasteel Pvt. Ltd., Bhadrashree Steel and Power Ltd., Baba Akhila Sai Jyothi Industries, ILC Iron and Steels Pvt. Ltd. and S.K. Steel Tech Pvt. Ltd.
These units are located in and around Hirebaganala, Halavarthi, Chikkabaganala and Kunikeri villages.
The joint action forum, however, urged the district administration to ensure strict implementation of the closure orders.

It demanded that the Deputy Commissioner immediately enforce the seizure orders and take steps to ensure that the units remain permanently closed. The forum cautioned that merely issuing closure orders will serve little purpose if the companies approach courts and obtain stay orders, as in the past.

According to the forum, 28 large and mega industrial units, including sponge iron, pellet, casting, steel, coke beneficiation, cement, chemical fertiliser, pesticide, acid and coal-based power generation units, have been operating in the region for nearly three decades. It said that these industries have been discharging excessive pollutants and industrial waste, affecting agriculture and public health in 22 villages.

The forum recalled that Sri Gavisiddeshwara Swamiji joined the campaign about a year and eight months ago demanding the cancellation of the proposed large-scale Baldota project and also, seeking strict pollution control measures in the existing industries. It said that the failure of the industries to comply with pollution control requirements has led to an increase in illnesses and deaths in the affected villages.

The joint action forum said that it launched an agitation on October 31, 2025 and organised three shutdown protests. It said that the Pollution Control Board has been compelled to issue the latest closure orders following the sustained agitation.

It pointed out that on an earlier occasion, closure orders were issued against five industrial units but, the board failed to file caveats in courts. As a result, three units obtained stay orders from courts and continued their operations. The forum warned that the same situation can recur unless the authorities take immediate legal and administrative steps to enforce the latest orders.

The forum said that nearly 50,000 people in the surrounding rural areas and 1.5 lakh residents of the twin cities affected by industrial pollution deserve a healthy environment. It warned that failure to ensure permanent closure of the polluting units will force people to intensify their agitation for a prolonged period.

articles.title: Delhi Police take key accused Prashanth into custody in ₹2-crore spurious drugs racket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a fresh development in the spurious drugs racket case in Karnataka, the Delhi Police have taken key accused Prashanth into custody in connection with a separate ₹2-crore cheating case registered against him in Delhi.

Prashanth is accused of cheating a Delhi-based person of ₹2 crore on the promise of supplying medicines. An FIR was registered against him at the Motilal Bagh Police Station in Delhi, following which police had been searching for him.

After a Special Investigation Team (SIT) arrested Prashanth in connection with the spurious drugs racket, Delhi Police approached the court and secured his custody through a body warrant. The Motilal Bagh police subsequently took Prashanth into their custody and are questioning him in connection with the alleged ₹2-crore fraud.

According to police sources in Bengaluru, Prashanth had a thriving business supplying spurious drugs across the country from his base in Tavarekere on the outskirts of Bengaluru. Following a raid on his godown by authorities in Karnataka in August earlier this year, he fled to Azerbaijan and was eventually arrested by the Bengaluru Police when he returned in September.

articles.title: YSRCP’s vote bank remains intact, says former MLA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tale Bhadrayya predicts victory in Rajam municipal polls; says party will regain its glory in 2029 Assembly elections

Former Palakonda MLA and YSRCP senior leader Tale Bhadrayya on Sunday said that the party’s vote bank remained intact despite the political challenges it had been facing in municipal and rural local body elections. He said the YSRCP secured nearly 40% of the votes in the 2024 general elections and polled around 35% in the recent elections despite what he termed the misuse of the administration by the Chandrababu Naidu government.
Speaking to the media in Rajam, he expressed confidence that the YSRCP would win the Rajam municipality elections scheduled for November 26, 2026.

“Although the YSRCP suffered defeats in the recent MPTC, ZPTC and municipal elections, it will win the Rajam municipality election, which was postponed due to legal and administrative issues,” he said.

Mr. Bhadrayya, who was elected from the neighbouring Palakonda Assembly constituency on a TDP ticket in 1985 and 1994, joined the YSRCP along with his son Tale Rajesh, the party’s Rajam constituency in-charge, ahead of the 2024 Assembly elections.

He said the YSRCP would regain its former glory in the 2029 Assembly elections. People, including beneficiaries of welfare schemes, would be able to exercise their franchise without fear as the elections would be conducted directly by the Central Election Commission, he added.

articles.title: Call to restore pedestrian access to walking paths in the Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Coonoor Consumer Protection Association has appealed to the Nilgiris Collector to remove encroachments on footpaths and restore pedestrian access to walking paths in towns across the district.

“In major towns across the Nilgiris district, including Ooty, Coonoor, Kotagiri, Gudalur, Pandalur and Manjoor, footpaths have been extensively encroached upon, forcing members of the public, including senior citizens, children and tourists, to walk on the roads at the risk of their lives,” the association said in a letter addressed to the Collector. It pointed out that the Madras High Court had issued an order on November 13 directing the submission of a compliance report by the government by December 10.

The association appealed to the Collector to remove all the encroachments from footpaths, restore the footpaths for public use, take preventative steps to ensure that encroachments do not return and conduct regular monitoring to maintain pedestrian access.

articles.title: HC judge’s reference to ‘harassment’ of Kallakurichi Collector triggers call for action against TVK MLA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: At a Gender Sensitisation Committee and Internal Complaints Committee (GSICC) - II meeting in Madurai on Saturday, Justice S. Victoria Gowri of the Madras High Court, said “When high ranking officers themselves were insecure, one can imagine the plight of ordinary persons.”

Days after the National Commission for Women (NCW) had written to the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police seeking a probe into the alleged harassment of Kallakurichi District Collector J.E. Padmaja by the Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh, a sitting judge of the Madras High Court raised the issue in a public platform, triggering fresh calls for action in the issue.

At a Gender Sensitisation Committee and Internal Complaints Committee (GSICC) - II meeting in Madurai on Saturday, Justice S. Victoria Gowri of the Madras High Court, said awareness camps were essential as safety in work places remained a big issue. “When high ranking officers themselves were insecure, one can imagine the plight of ordinary persons,” she said.

Justice Gowri then said, “Now, the Kallakurichi Collector...A sitting MLA sends an obscene message to her. Isn’t that workplace harassment? Her husband files a complaint. Till now the police working under this State government remains indifferent. With that question, through this programme in our big family, today we are going to see how our brothers and sisters shall work amicably and comfortably.”

In the wake of the judge’s remarks, Henri Tiphagne, executive director of People’s Watch, a civil rights group, on Sunday said Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should have acted on this issue. “The serious allegation of harassment of a serving women officer is highly condemnable. The Chief Minister should have directed the police to inquire and file a case, if the allegations were found to be true....Remaining silent does not solve, but only creates suspicion among the right thinking people about the promises [of women safety] made by the TVK leaders,” he told The Hindu .

An advocate, who participated in the GSICC meeting, said it was baffling that the police had not yet registered a case in this regard, “despite a complaint being lodged on behalf of the Kallakurichi Collector”. [There has been no formal confirmation yet of a complaint having been filed.] The state police are definitely accountable, especially, when the issue had been raised by none other than a serving High Court Judge at a gender sensitisation awareness camp, the advocate said.

AIADMK senior leader R.B. Udayhakumar, in a statement, said the party’s stand on the issue had been vindicated. “None other than a High Court judge has expressed concern over the safety of women. The TVK leaders were hurriedly denying the allegations. People in responsible positions like the judge had specifically pointed out the issue. This showed the negligence of the Chief Minister,” he said.
“The people should realise how insensitive this government handled sensitive issues,” he said and urged the State Commission for Women to take up the case suo motu.
A day after the remarks by the judge, AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Sunday urged the court to take suo motu cognisance of the allegations.

In a social media post, Mr. Dhinakaran criticised Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for “failing” to initiate action against the MLA despite the seriousness of the complaint. He questioned why the Chief Minister was quick to order police action against critics of the government but remained silent when allegations were levelled against a member of his own party.

Pointing out that the NCW had sought an explanation from the Tamil Nadu police over the issue, Mr. Dhinakaran alleged double standards in the government’s approach to complaints against ruling party members. He also raised concerns over women’s safety, police accountability, and equality before the law.
Mr. Dhinakaran urged the court to ensure the allegations were properly investigated and appropriate legal action taken.

articles.title: Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

Myanmar has termed the ASEAN leaders' assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan "unfair and imbalanced", accusing the regional bloc of disregarding its views and denying it equal rights and representation as a member state.

In a statement issued on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila on November 15, 2026 did not adequately reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country.

"Although ASEAN has yet to reach a consensus, Myanmar continues to engage bilaterally with individual ASEAN Member states," the Ministry said, expressing appreciation to members that had extended support and assistance in recognition of what it described as positive developments in the country.

The statement comes after ASEAN leaders reiterated their concern over insufficient progress in implementing the five-point peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 following the military takeover in Myanmar.
They also extended restrictions on the country's leadership attending the bloc's summits, saying the ban would remain until there was meaningful progress in implementing the plan.
Under the arrangement, Myanmar can be represented at ASEAN summits only by a non-political representative, such as a career diplomat.

The five-point consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, an ASEAN special envoy to facilitate mediation, a visit by the envoy to Myanmar to meet all parties, and humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management.

The conflict in Myanmar has continued since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, triggering widespread protests, a military crackdown and an armed resistance movement.

ASEAN's five-point consensus was adopted in April 2021 in an attempt to end the violence and facilitate a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the bloc has repeatedly expressed frustration over the lack of progress in its implementation.
Rejecting criticism of its handling of the conflict, Myanmar said it had continued to cooperate with ASEAN's suggestions and recommendations while safeguarding its national interests and sovereignty.
The Ministry asserted that "there are no political prisoners" in the country, maintaining that individuals were serving sentences under existing laws.

The statement also defended the government's security operations, saying it had undertaken only measures necessary to safeguard the country's sovereignty and protect its people, while exercising "utmost restraint" and employing minimum force in accordance with domestic laws and applicable Rules of Engagement.

articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight.
For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost.

Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado.

“They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.”
It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way.

Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages.

In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts.

Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened.

One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.

In addition to the Phans, The Associated Press interviewed six other people familiar with the treatment of detainees in South Sudan, including relatives and lawyers. Most spoke on condition of anonymity for fear of retaliation against the detainees.
AP also reviewed money-transfer receipts and messages between guards and four detainees' relatives.

When asked about AP' s findings, a spokesperson from South Sudan's Foreign Ministry said detainees are given adequate food, water and medical care, and are allowed regular contact with relatives and lawyers while it works to resolve their individual cases. The spokesperson said the Government pays for all the associated costs.

articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time
The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time.
Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”.

“We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale.

The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien.

Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments.

“We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name.
Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP .

Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive. The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.

The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal. “This text isn’t a climate plan. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.

The summit had been under pressure to show progress on tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Türkiye and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, such as diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives.

The draft calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, and the expansion of “clean energy”. But it does not explicitly require that electrification be powered by renewable energy. About one-third of global electricity is produced using coal, and another fifth using fossil gas.

Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale.

The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien.

Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments.

“We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name.

Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP .

Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive. The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.

The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal. “This text isn’t a climate plan. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.

The summit had been under pressure to show progress on tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Türkiye and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, such as diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives.

The draft calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, and the expansion of “clean energy”. But it does not explicitly require that electrification be powered by renewable energy. About one-third of global electricity is produced using coal, and another fifth using fossil gas.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The draft calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, and the expansion of “clean energy”. But it does not explicitly require that electrification be powered by renewable energy. About one-third of global electricity is produced using coal, and another fifth using fossil gas.

articles.title: Rebels kill 15 in South Sudan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: An official hinted at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025
An attack on Sunday (November 22, 2026) by rebels in northwestern South Sudan has killed at least 15 civilians, with the toll likely to rise, local sources told AFP .
One official pointed the finger at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025.

“The attack on the Bol Bol Boma area in Tonj East County, Warrap State, began late on Saturday,” Machuei Bith, the county's caretaker commissioner, told AFP . He blamed the deaths on fighters from neighbouring Unity State belonging to Machar's SPLA-IO armed group.

"Fifteen civilians and cattle keepers were killed and four armed attackers with SPLA-IO uniforms were also killed," he told AFP . A local police officer confirmed the story on condition of anonymity and said the fighting was still ongoing on Sunday morning. "Further details on casualties from both sides will be shared later on with the media," the officer said.
23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces

Since independence from Sudan in 2011, the world's youngest country has been forced to grapple with various violent conflicts, linked to political infighting, ethnic tensions or competition for resources.
Between 2013 and 2018, the eastern African country was torn apart by a civil war pitting forces loyal to Machar against those supporting Kiir, which left more than 4,00,000 people dead.

articles.title: Traffic management, not enforcement, will be our priority: Bengaluru Traffic Commissioner
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hemant M. Nimbalkar says officers must focus on managing traffic rather than enforcement, and that no vehicle should be stopped unless there is a visible violation

The restructuring of the Bengaluru City Police administration has also resulted in a dedicated Commissioner for Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP), even as the five Commissioners will oversee traffic in their respective jurisdictions at the local level. This, it is argued, will bring together ground-level implementation and city-level planning.
Hemant M. Nimbalkar, the new Traffic Commissioner, Bengaluru, speaks to The Hindu about his plans to tackle the city’s notorious traffic gridlocks. Edited excerpts
The Hindu: Bengaluru’s traffic congestion is notorious and you have the challenge to beat it. What will be your first move?

Hemant Nimbalkar: We see very few of our officers on the road and this needs to change. Henceforth, even senior officials including Deputy Commissioners of Police (DCPs) will have to be on the roads during peak hours. A junction chart, like a beat system for the law and order police, will be drawn up and this will serve as a roster for officers to take turns managing traffic at junctions. Our office needs to be the road.
TH: Will this also mean an increase in contact enforcement? Citizens are already complaining about harassment by the police on the road.

HN: No. Officers have to focus on managing traffic first, not enforcement. No vehicle should be stopped unless there is a visible violation. For instance, anyone riding without a helmet or driving on the wrong side of the road has to be stopped because it is a safety issue. The practice of stopping vehicles at officers’ will will stop.
TH: There has been an argument that the enforcement is not punitive enough to create deterrence among violators. How will you address that?
HN: Traffic violations that endanger human lives will be dealt with seriously.
TH: There are concerns over dual reporting structure for traffic management in the new setup. Will this create any confusion?

HN: There is no confusion. Traffic management is both local and pan-city at the same time. Each of the five commissionerates has traffic divisions that will be monitored by the respective Commissioners. This decentralisation will help the city with more pragmatic local solutions. But traffic is also dynamic, and congestion in one part has an impact on another. That is where city-level leadership, the Traffic Management Centre and the deployment of technology come in.

HN: Congestion cannot be beaten through traffic management alone. But from our side, we will take a holistic approach to identify the reasons for congestion at a given point. Traffic personnel standing at a signal are not in charge of just that signal, but a stretch of 300–500 metres before that. The move to station senior officers at junctions during peak hours will help us better understand the reasons for congestion at any point. For instance, illegal parking, driving on one-way roads and other violations also contribute to congestion. Better enforcement along the stretch will help us ease congestion to some extent.
For this, we need a combination of artificial intelligence, big data analytics, human intelligence and human effort, which will be my approach to managing Bengaluru’s traffic.

articles.title: Congress will return to power in Telangana for second term with 90 seats and one crore votes: Revanth Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has expressed confidence that the Congress will return to power in Telangana for a second consecutive term, asserting that the party would win 90 Assembly seats with one crore votes in the next elections.

Addressing the Extended Executive Committee meeting of the Telangana Congress on Sunday, he said the party leadership was preparing strategies to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots and take the government’s welfare and development initiatives to the people after Sankranti.

Recalling the party’s difficult days when he took over as Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the BRS leadership had allegedly used coercion and police cases to force several Congress MLAs and leaders to join the ruling party. Former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekhar Rao had even declared that there was no Congress in Telangana and that he would not allow the party to revive, he said.

However, the Congress undertook a digital membership drive and enrolled 48 lakh members in 90 days, the highest by any party in the country. This resulted in Congress securing 92,35,833 votes and won 64 Assembly seats in the last elections.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said the Congress had rewarded those who worked for the organisation citing the examples of Adluri Laxman Kumar, Aadi Srinivas, Medipalli Satyam, Kavvampalli Satyanarayana, Vakiti Srihari and Makkan Singh Raj Thakur.

The Chief Minister cautioned party leaders against expecting positions merely by moving around Gandhi Bhavan or visiting Delhi. “The place to go is not Delhi but villages and the homes of the poor,” he said.

He said the party was closely monitoring the conduct and public statements of its leaders, including what they said in public and behind the scenes. The political balance sheet would be prepared once every five years, at election time, and the contribution of every leader and worker would be assessed.
Taking a dig at BRS leaders, he said the party’s claims of returning to power were misplaced. Congress would counter the BRS campaign by taking its achievements to the people.

He urged Telangana Congress leaders to take responsibility for making Rahul Gandhi the Prime Minister and said the party would aim to win all 15 Lok Sabha seats in the State. Telangana had stood by the Congress during its difficult periods, including the period following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, who was representing Medak as an MP at the time, he said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar on Sunday inaugurated an 11 kV solar panel system installed at the local Gurudwara using MPLADS funds in Karimnagar.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sanjay said the Gurudwara had been incurring an electricity bill of approximately ₹25,000 every month, which had become a financial burden on its management. The solar power system was installed using MPLADS funds to ease the financial burden, he said.
Mr. Sanjay lauded the Sikh community’s contribution to India’s freedom struggle and the armed forces, describing its sacrifices and patriotism as invaluable and unforgettable.

He alleged that Pakistan was aiding and abetting the smuggling of drugs into Punjab and targeting young people to lure them into drug addiction as part of a conspiracy to weaken the country and promote terrorism. “We should remain vigilant and foil Pakistan’s evil designs,” he said.
He called upon people to extend their support to the Central government’s Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, aimed at combating drug abuse and addiction.

articles.title: Vijayawada Mayor, 86 corporators to take oath today
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: All arrangements are in place for the conduct of the oath-taking ceremony of the Mayor and corporators of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC), scheduled to be held at the Dr. Ambedkar Kala Vedika in Vijayawada on Monday.

A large number of supporters are expected to take part in the ceremony, which is being held outside the VMC council hall after a long time, as the NDA alliance won the municipal elections in the city with a thumping majority. The NDA emerged victorious in 76 out of 86 divisions, while YSRCP won 8 of them. The remaining two were won by an independent candidate and CPI(M) corporator.

Initially, while all the eight YSRCP corporators had decided to boycott the ceremony, expressing objection to the choice of the venue, they later withdrew their boycott call. They had said it was a long-standing tradition to hold the ceremony at the VMC council hall. But, as per latest information, the YSRCP corporators have withdrawn their call and are expected to take part in the ceremony at the new venue.
The lone corporator from the CPI(M), Boye Satya Babu, said while the venue itself does not matter, but he questioned as to who would bear the expenses of the ceremony.

After the oath-taking ceremony is over, the candidate for the post of the Deputy Mayor is also likely to be announced. While more than five names are doing the rounds, the final decision is likely to be announced by the party high command on Monday. Ummadi Venkateswara Rao, Adduri Sriram, Nellibandla Balaswamy, Chennupati Usha Rani, Chennupati Kanthi Sri, Jasti Sambasiva Rao, Devineni Nagamahita are a few names being talked about. All these, except for Mr. Sriram, belong to the Telugu Desam Party.

articles.title: Jana Sena activist dies during clash over panchayat nominations in Pulivendula
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pawan Kalyan orders an inquiry into the sequence of events that led to the death

Munthala Veeranjaneyulu, a Jana Sena Party (JSP) activist, died of a heart attack in the melee witnessed during the scrutiny of nominations for the sarpanch elections in Nagulaguttapalli village of Pulivendula constituency in YSR Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh , on Saturday (November 21, 2026) night.
Tense moments were witnessed, with the rival parties engaged in a war of words, even as the nominations were being scrutinised.
Though the cause of death was heart attack, the enraged local Jana Sena activists blamed the TDP for the melee, with the spread of fake news on social media.

Though the situation that actually led to the clamour is not yet clear, highly placed sources said that the Jana Sena workers were reportedly misled by the YSRCP campaigners to revolt against the TDP, which led to the clashes.

నాగులగుట్టపల్లి ఘటనపై నిష్పక్షపాత విచారణకు ఉప ముఖ్యమంత్రివర్యులు శ్రీ @PawanKalyan గారు దిశా నిర్దేశం • నామినేషన్ల పరిశీలన సందర్భంలో జనసైనికుడు శ్రీ ముంతల రామాంజులు మృతి ఘటనపై ఆరా • శ్రీ రామాంజులు కుటుంబానికి అన్ని విధాలా అండగా ఉంటామని భరోసా పులివెందుల నియోజకవర్గం, చక్రాయపేట మండలం, సురభి గ్రామ పంచాయతీ పరిధిలోని నాగులగుట్టపల్లి వద్ద నామినేషన్ల పరిశీలన సందర్భంగా చోటుచేసుకున్న వివాదంలో జనసేన మద్దతుతో సర్పంచ్ గా పోటీ చేస్తున్న అభ్యర్థి బంధువు, జనసేన కార్యకర్త శ్రీ ముంతల రామాంజులు గుండెపోటుతో మరణించిన ఘటనపై రాష్ట్ర ఉప ముఖ్యమంత్రివర్యులు, జనసేన పార్టీ అధ్యక్షులు శ్రీ పవన్ కళ్యాణ్ గారు తీవ్రంగా స్పందించారు. ఘటనపై జిల్లా యంత్రాంగం, పార్టీ శ్రేణుల నుంచి వివరాలు తెలుసుకున్నారు. నామినేషన్ల పరిశీలన సమయంలో చోటుచేసుకున్న పరిణామాలు, ఆ సమయంలో అక్కడ నెలకొన్న పరిస్థితులపై సమగ్ర వివరాలు సేకరించాలని కడప జిల్లా కలెక్టర్, ఎస్పీలకు సూచించారు. ఈ ఘటనపై నిష్పక్షపాతంగా, పారదర్శకంగా విచారణ జరపాలన్నారు. మృతుడు శ్రీ ముంతల రామాంజులు కుటుంబ సభ్యుల వాంగ్మూలాలను నమోదు చేసి, ఘటనకు సంబంధించిన అన్ని అంశాలను క్షుణ్ణంగా పరిశీలించాలని దిశానిర్దేశం చేశారు. విచారణలో ఎవరైనా బాధ్యులుగా తేలితే, వారిపై నిబంధనల ప్రకారం కఠిన చర్యలు తీసుకోవాలని కోరారు. •విచారణ ప్రక్రియపై మంత్రివర్యులు శ్రీ నాదెండ్ల మనోహర్ గారి ప్రత్యేక పర్యవేక్షణ పులివెందుల జనసైనికుడి మృతి, క్షేత్ర స్థాయిలో చోటు చేసుకున్న పరిస్థితులపై విచారించాలని పార్టీ పీఏసీ ఛైర్మన్, రాష్ట్ర ఆహార పౌర సరఫరాల శాఖ మంత్రి శ్రీ నాదెండ్ల మనోహర్ గారికి సూచించారు. విచారణ ప్రక్రియను సమన్వయం చేస్తూ, పురోగతిని ఎప్పటికప్పుడు సమీక్షించాలని తెలిపారు. శ్రీ రామాంజులు కుటుంబానికి పార్టీ తరఫన భరోసా ఇచ్చేందుకు రాష్ట్ర పోలీస్ హౌసింగ్ కార్పొరేషన్ ఛైర్మన్‌ శ్రీ కళ్యాణం శివశ్రీనివాస్ ను పులివెందులకు పంపారు. స్థానిక సంస్థల ఎన్నికల వేళ శ్రీ ముంతల రామాంజులు ప్రాణాలు కోల్పోవడం పట్ల ఉప ముఖ్యమంత్రివర్యులు విచారం వ్యక్తం చేశారు. ఆయన కుటుంబాన్ని పార్టీ తరఫున అన్ని విధాలా ఆదుకుంటామని స్పష్టం చేశారు.

Several cars of TDP leaders were damaged and their windscreens shattered in the violence that followed late at night. TDP constituency in-charge Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy (B.Tech Ravi), who paid respects to the mortal remains of Veeranjaneyulu on Sunday, appealed to the cadres not to believe the rumours.

On coming to know of the development, party president K. Pawan Kalyan directed the party programmes committee chairman and AP Police Housing Development Corporation chairman Kalyanam Siva Srinivasa Rao to submit a report on the sequence of incidents that led to the death.
Following this, Mr. Rao rushed to Pulivendula on Sunday.

Several cars of TDP leaders were damaged and their windscreens shattered in the violence that followed late at night. articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia
“Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

"The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied.

Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added.

The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X.
OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.
The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

“Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

articles.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted,’ COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing session

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies.

Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.

But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”.

On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu.

Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.

Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

On Friday (November 20, 2026), Mr. Eisenkot warned that he would not allow the talks to drag on, saying he was ready to submit to parliament an “emergency national government”. Although he did not spell out how, his statements suggest a two-stage plan: the swift formation of a minority government based on the core opposition parties, and then broadening it.

A minority Eisenkot government could receive support from the 19 Arab party lawmakers, but his right-wing ally Avigdor Liberman rejects working with them, and instead advocates an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

articles.title: Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month.

Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said.

Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television.

“He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament.

“My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping.
Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”.

“That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”.
“We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.
Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

articles.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company.

Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported.

The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang.

Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully.
Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure.

The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company.

Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported.

The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang.

Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully.

Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure.

The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Riyadh denounces ‘criminal’ attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.

Bahrain on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said two people were wounded in an Iranian attack on Saturday (November 21, 2026) against “a civilian industrial site” in the kingdom, which has repeatedly come under attack in recent days.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September.
“In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain... a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded,” Bahrain’s Interior Ministry said on X.
“His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition. Both are being treated in hospital.”
Two residents told AFP they had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco.

In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked with missiles and drones U.S. Patriot air defence systems at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Tehran said on Saturday it had intercepted a U.S. drone targeting Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic maritime corridor at the heart of the war in West Asia.

Bahrain’s powerful neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday lambasted Tehran for its continued “brutal aggression” against Gulf countries. In a statement published on X, the Saudi Foreign Ministry expressed “the strongest condemnation and denunciation by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain”.

Saudi Arabia also announced early on Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis in the west of the kingdom. The region is home to key energy infrastructure, including the oil terminal at the port of Yanbu, as well as the Jizan refinery, located in the far southwest of the country, near the border with Yemen.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen’s civil war this summer, the latest front in the West Asia war.

Later on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen said it had “intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the Houthis” toward the greater Riyadh region, which is regularly shaken by explosions.

Since the conflict in Yemen resumed in July, the Houthis have multiplied attacks on Saudi Arabia, particularly since October, targeting its major oil installations and airports in particular. They have also repeatedly struck the financial district of the capital, Riyadh.
