articles.title: ASHAs reject government’s assurance; decide to continue protest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The talks failed after Health Minister U.T. Khader said the demand for an increase in remuneration would be discussed during the preparation of the next State Budget

The second round of talks between the State government and protesting ASHAs ended inconclusively on Saturday, with the workers rejecting the government’s assurance on a pay hike and deciding to continue their agitation, which entered its fifth day.

Health Minister U.T. Khader had invited representatives of the Karnataka State Samyukta ASHA Workers’ Union for discussions. The delegation included union president K. Somashekar, secretary D. Nagalakshmi and other office-bearers.

The talks failed after the Minister said the demand for an increase in remuneration would be discussed during the preparation of the next State Budget. The workers refused to accept the assurance and decided to continue their protest.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to the protesting ASHAs to withdraw their agitation, expressing sympathy for their hardships and acknowledging their contribution to the healthcare system.
Mr. Shivakumar said the government was considering a comprehensive and lasting solution to their demands and would discuss the matter with the Cabinet before taking an appropriate decision.

“Please respond to my appeal and withdraw your agitation. We respect your service, hard work and sacrifice. The government is committed to addressing your demands and finding an appropriate solution,” he said, appealing to the workers.

articles.title: Skywalk, flyover planned at Konanakunte Cross
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government is planning both a skywalk and a flyover at the busy Konanakunte Cross, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said. “Pedestrian movement has increased with the metro station and the traffic has also shot up,” he said, directing officials to plan a skywalk at the junction to ensure safe and convenient connectivity for pedestrians. He also asked them to ensure that it did not affect or obstruct the proposed flyover construction.

Earlier this year, the special purpose vehicle, Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE), obtained government approval to construct a flyover at the junction, citing increasing traffic volumes that had led to congestion even on connecting roads.
Mr. Gowda said the tendering process for the project is currently underway. He made the announcement after inaugurating the third phase of the Ward One Campaign at Konanakunte Cross on Saturday.

“B-SMILE has prepared a plan to construct a split-type flyover, with elevated stretches of approximately 600 metres on either side of the junction. The project, including flyover construction and land acquisition, is estimated to cost around ₹77 crore,” Mr. Gowda said, adding that officials had been directed to expedite the process and commence work at the earliest.
According to documents available with The Hindu , the SPV had estimated the cost of the entire project at nearly ₹291 crore.
“Once completed, the flyover will facilitate signal-free movement through this stretch, significantly easing the traffic congestion currently faced by motorists,” Mr. Gowda said.

The Minister said the civic body is upgrading footpaths, providing clearly marked zebra crossings, and undertaking road and side marking works to ensure better traffic discipline and safer pedestrian movement. “To further ease vehicular movement, officials have been instructed to secure a portion of Metro-owned land near Forum Mall to create a free-left turn,” he said.

The Ward One Campaign, aimed at identifying and resolving civic infrastructure issues at the ward level, has covered 83 wards in the first two phases. The civic bodies will cover another 41 wards in the third phase.

Under the campaign, specific wards are identified within each municipal corporation, and issues relating to roads, footpaths, street lighting, tree branch clearance, potholes and garbage management are addressed through coordinated interventions.

“Although the campaign was initially scheduled to be completed by November, it will now continue into December to ensure that sanitation and other improvement works are carried out effectively at the grassroots level,” he said.

articles.title: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer test website to earn money: Sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu .
The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces.

“Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said.
During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money.

“He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined.

After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database.

The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach.

The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised.

While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said.
As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action.

articles.title: TGSPDCL sub-engineer caught taking ₹30,000 bribe in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A sub-engineer of the Telangana Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TGSPDCL) was caught red-handed by the Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) while allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹30,000 at the complainant’s residence in Hyderabad on Saturday, November 21.

The accused, G. Santosh Anand, sub-engineer at the Gandhi Nagar Section Office of TGSPDCL, had initially demanded ₹50,000 from the complainant and subsequently reduced the amount to ₹35,000 before settling for ₹30,000. The bribe was demanded in return for showing official favour by not taking any further action against the complainant in connection with an allegation of electricity theft.

During the trap operation, the accused counted the bribe amount and kept the cash in the left-side back pocket of his trousers. The ACB officials subsequently recovered the tainted money from his pocket. He was arrested and would be produced before the Special Court for SPE and ACB Cases in Hyderabad for judicial remand. The case is under investigation.

articles.title: Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.

Prices of prominent metals including gold, copper and aluminium tumbled to at least seven-month lows on hawkish commentary about U.S. Fed seeking to increase rates and weighing concerns over global economic growth in the immediate term.
Benchmark price of the yellow metal, that is, at the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) slipped to their lowest since September 2025 to close this week at $3,521.38 per troy ounce.
Further, benchmark price of copper – that is, at the London Metal Exchange (LME) – slipped to their lowest in about eight months at $12,230.40 per metric tonne.
Reference price for aluminium at LME also slipped to an almost one-year low at $2,824.5 per metric tonne.

Gold prices in 2026 have taken a nosedive from where they began the year, with the yellow metal falling over 25% from its peak, with a majority of the unwinding taking place over the last couple of months. Gold has seen exponential growth since 2022, rising 145% globally till now, with prices hitting multiple record highs last year.
Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Limited, says the primary driver of the downswing in gold prices is the change in global macroeconomic conditions.

“The biggest driver (in price movements) is that the macro story changed. Since the (Iran-U.S.) war, inflation expectations, energy prices, and anticipation of interest rate hikes capped gains for the metal.”

With traders expecting a more hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, the U.S. dollar has also gained strength in recent weeks. It is important to note that gold typically thrives in a weak-dollar environment.
U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s remarks last week further cemented expectations of a rate hike next month.
According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the target range to 4.00–4.25%.

Further, rising US Treasury yields have also added pressure on gold prices. Since gold is a non-interest-bearing asset, higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding the precious metal, making yield-bearing assets relatively more attractive.

Gold analysts expect the metal to trade range-bound over the next couple of quarters and into the beginning of FY28. The precious metal is expected to trade between $3,200 and $3,800 in the near term.

articles.title: Zelenskiy says China summit was ‘very unsuccessful’ for Russia

fullParagraphs: The Ukrainian President said Vladimir Putin had failed to recreate the Yalta conference, and that it is not clear to Kyiv whether it will be able to join NATO

articles.title: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor”

Finland’s military detected a drone attack on Saturday morning (November 21, 2026) on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, which caused the vessel to catch fire, the Nordic country’s authorities said.

The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message on X: “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.”
Fighting off a Russian invasion now in its fifth year, Ukraine has stepped up its long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

“On Saturday morning, the Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against a Russian cargo vessel west of Suursaari, in the eastern Gulf of Finland, in international waters,” the Ministry said in a statement.
According to Finnish border guards dispatched to the scene the ship caught fire and began drifting towards Finnish waters after the strike.
“The situation currently poses no danger to other vessels,” the border service said in a press release.
Authorities gave no immediate details of the boat’s crew.
Finland immediately informed NATO of the strike, the Defence Ministry said.
It said temporary restrictions were enforced in the airspace and maritime area of the eastern part of the Gulf.
The Baltic Sea has become a potential flashpoint in the wake of Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with Western countries accusing Moscow of conducting a “hybrid war” in the strategic waterway.
Lying at the easternmost end of the Baltic along the coasts of Finland, Estonia and Russia, the Gulf of Finland is a key maritime passage for Russia, leading to the former capital, Saint Petersburg.

articles.title: MHA sanctions more Central forces for Tripura municipal elections

fullParagraphs: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura slated for November 27. State Election Commissioner (SEC) Pradip Chakraborty said the MHA has informed the State government of its decision on Saturday.

He added that with local availability of the CAPF, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed on election duties. The deployment will remain in force even after the declaration of results on December 2.

The Opposition CPI(M) and Congress have long been demanding adequate deployment of Central forces alleging that the ruling BJP is trying to turn the elections into a farce through gross irregularities and use of government machinery. They have accused the State police of failing to discharge duties neutrally.

The SEC had announced a schedule to hold elections for 21 ULBs including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC). However, the Congress and CPI(M) said clamed their candidates were prevented from filing nomination papers for five civic bodies.
The BJP secured victory in five ULBs unopposed and hence, the polls will technically occur in 16 areas instead of 21.

With the election campaign picking up pace, Opposition parties have alleged that their supporters are facing obstacles and threats during the door-to-door campaign. The parties have also sought the attention of the authorities after spotting several masked youth taking part in an campaign procession of the BJP in Agartala on Saturday. They alleged the youth may have been brought in from outside the State.

articles.title: Kannada writer Ravi Hanj tracked to Kochi airport, served notice to appear for probe amid Basava Mantapa book controversy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ravi Hanj was detained during security checks while attempting to travel abroad, say Kerala Police sources.

Kannada writer Ravi Hanj, who is at the centre of a major controversy over alleged derogatory remarks against 12th-century social reformer Basavanna in his book Basava Mantapa and in interviews around the book , was tracked down to Cochin International Airport in Keralam. He was stopped by Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel while attempting to travel abroad.
The CISF stopped Mr. Hanj acting on a lookout notice issued against him by the Belagavi police. There are four FIRs pending against him in Bengaluru, Belagavi, Bagewadi, and Vijayapura.

“He [Ravi Hunj] initially attempted to create the impression that he had left India for the United States. However, verification by the Home Department established that he was in a neighbouring State. He has been traced and a formal notice has been issued directing him to appear before the investigating authorities,” said Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge.
Sources said the Karnataka Police have questioned him and the Bengaluru City Police have served him a notice to appear before them for questioning before November 24, Tuesday.

“Since Mr. Hanj is a U.S. citizen, we have also formally informed the U.S. Embassy about the FIR registered against him and the requirement for his questioning in connection with the investigation. Foreign citizenship does not place anyone above Indian law. It also does not provide immunity from investigation or accountability,” Mr. Kharge said.

The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday decided to forfeit his book following complaints by Veerashiva-Lingayat groups. The book’s publisher, Vishweshwar Bhat, has also been named in the Bengaluru and Vijayapura FIRs. The book is a compilation of columns published in the Viswavani newspaper under the same title Basava Mantapa . It was released as a book in Bengaluru on November 15.

Speaking to presspersons later, Mr. Hanj said that he respects the law of the land. “Ministers are involved in the action against me. So I do not have confidence that the investigation will be fair. But I will continue my legal fight,” he said.

articles.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

“For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said.

Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”.

It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.

The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

articles.title: Adopt best practices from ‘Maha Kumbh Meal’ for conduct of Godavari Pushkaralu, CM tells officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He approves construction of a temple for Lord Surya and Brihaspati in Rajamahendravaram at a cost of ₹1.80 crore and instructs officials to focus on crowd control and regulating vehicular traffic
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has suggested to the officials to adopt the best practices followed in the Maha Kumbh Mela , for the successful conduct of Godavari Pushkaralu.

In a review meeting on the arrangements being made for the mega event on Saturday, Mr. Naidu said ‘Jala Harathi’ was being initiated throughout the State starting with the Godavari River, and called for an apt name to the mega religious event.

He called for preparation of estimates of the water flow levels in the Godavari River in June to take necessary steps for safety. Besides, he approved the construction of a temple for Lord Surya (Sun God) and Brihaspati (Jupiter) in Rajamahendravaram at a cost of ₹1.80 crore.
He ordered improvement of road connectivity from Pattiseema to Polavaram and Kovvur to Dowleswaram, steps to obtain clearance for upgradation of the Polavaram bridge.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that development of 78 roads had been undertaken at a cost of ₹300 crore and they would be completed by April 2027.

Mr. Naidu instructed the officials to duly focus on crowd control and regulating vehicular traffic keeping in view the huge number of devotees who would be making a beeline for Rajamahendravaram and other nearby riverfronts.

Vijayawada, Rajamahendravaram and Visakhapatnam airports should be beautified on the occasion to welcome devotees arriving from across the country, he said, adding that the overall arrangements should be completed by March 2027.

articles.title: Reverse policies, stop tax sops for rich: Trade unions, farm outfits to PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Referring to the PM’s remarks at the recently-held Annual General Meeting of FCCI, farmers’ unions and trade groups say employment generation remains low despite tax cuts and incentives to corporate companies

Trade unions and farmers’ organisations on Saturday (November 21, 2026) demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi apologise to the people of the country for the “staggering failure” of the Make in India and Viksit Bharat 2047 projects and for “blindly following” neo-liberal policies that offered tax cuts and loan waivers to corporate houses.

The organisations were referring to Mr. Modi’s statement at the centenary Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) in New Delhi on November 19 that corporate companies failed to increase investment, generate employment and raise workers’ salaries despite successive tax concessions and incentives.

In a statement on Saturday (November 21, 2026), the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) said the Make in India initiative, launched in September 2014, targeted an increase in the manufacturing sector’s share of GDP from 16% in 2013-14 to 25% by 2021-22. Maintaining that the manufacturing share in the new GDP series is 13.3%, the SKM said unemployment has become the most burning issue in India today. “The failure of the Make in India initiative exposes the limitations of the centralised approach to industrial development and the false propaganda of self-reliance and Viksit Bharat 2047,” they said, adding that the Modi regime reduced the base corporate tax rate from 30% to 22% for existing domestic companies and 15% for new manufacturing firms.

“The demand for imposing a wealth tax was blatantly declined, and the education and health sectors were systematically dismantled. These pro-corporate policies have resulted in increasing inequality, de-industrialisation, and unbridled unemployment,” it added.

Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) general secretary Elamaram Kareem said in a statement that Mr. Modi’s acknowledgement vindicated the position consistently advanced by CITU that corporate tax concessions and incentives do not automatically translate into productive investment, employment generation or improvement in workers’ living standards.

“CITU has consistently opposed the Government’s supply-side, pro-corporate economic strategy, which relies on tax concessions, subsidies and incentives to stimulate private investment while neglecting people’s purchasing power,” Mr. Kareem said. “Corporate profits reached 4.8% of GDP in 2023-24, a 15-year high, growing by 22.3%, while employment grew by only 1.5%. Employee expenses of listed companies grew by just 13%, against 17% in the previous year,” he added, and demanded a “fundamental reversal” of the policy direction.

“The forthcoming Union Budget must abandon the approach of granting successive concessions to corporate capital and instead mobilise resources through progressive taxation. An effective wealth tax on the super-rich, inheritance/estate tax on large transfers of wealth and higher taxation of extraordinary corporate profits and massive wealth accumulation are essential,” he said.

articles.title: Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside Iran, he says, adding that ‘a fair solution’ could be reached; U.S. denies Iran fired at an F-16

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him.

Mr. Araghchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that Tehran was seeking “an agreement that would ensure there was no further war” and wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures.

The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the West Asia, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region.
The Foreign Minister said Iran’s red lines included keeping enriched uranium in the country, though he added that he believed “a fair solution” could be reached.
“They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me,” Mr. Trump said at a press conference on Friday.
The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to strike Israel and Gulf states hosting U.S. military bases.

Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in talks aimed at “bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground,” a spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said.

U.S. Central Command on Saturday (November 20, 2026) denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a U.S. F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing.
Iranian state media earlier reported that the country’s air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.
“Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement.

articles.title: Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality

Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies.

In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality.
The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend.

"The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said.
He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions.

Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations.

Sri Lanka's Human Rights Commission called for the Bill's withdrawal, while the Bar Association of Sri Lanka raised concerns about its impact on fundamental rights and safeguards for judicial oversight.

Rights body Amnesty International also called for its complete withdrawal, while the New York-based Human Rights Watch said the proposed legislation fell short of international human rights standards.

Rights groups have also raised concerns over extended detention, the admissibility of confessions made to senior police officers, restrictions on bail, police surveillance and searches and arrests without warrants.

Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies.

In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality.

The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend.

"The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said.

He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions.

Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20
Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat".
The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.

The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.

The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles".
The coalition also hit "military targets" in Sanaa, including missile and drone facilities and a supply depot, he said on X.

The Houthis said coalition strikes had killed 41 people in the previous 24 hours. Yemen's Saudi-backed armed forces said dozens of airstrikes and drone attacks, as well as hundreds of artillery attacks, killed or wounded 193 Houthi fighters.

articles.title: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack

An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians ​in a vehicle carrying papers and food for the World ⁠Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses said.
World Central Kitchen, an aid organisation that distributes food in the Gaza Strip, said, however, ‌that the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

The Israeli military said several militants had been targeted in the area without providing ‌further details. It did not immediately respond to questions on why ‌it ⁠had hit a vehicle that appeared to be distributing aid.
A ⁠Reuters witness said the vehicle appeared to be carrying packaged foodstuffs, and that papers inside carried World Central Kitchen's logo.
"It was just about to stop to distribute the food and ​drink to children when it was ‌hit by a missile," said Abu Zein Al-Daya, who witnessed the strike.
Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack.
The Israeli military killed seven World Central Kitchen workers ​in a 2024 strike, including citizens of Australia, Britain and Poland.
At the time, the military said there had been "serious errors and ⁠breaches of procedure" but in 2026 it said it had found no basis on which to open criminal investigations into the incident.
Israel briefly launched a ‌ground operation in Gaza earlier this week and killed six people in a strike on a hospital that it said was targeting a commander for the Palestinian militant group Hamas.
An October 2025 U.S.-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered territory but has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas' disarmament.
At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been ‌killed since then, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli troops now control around ​two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory ⁠along Gaza's coast.

articles.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington; It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland
A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday (November 21, 2026).

Meanwhile, a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday (November 21, 2026) after it was hit by drones, Finnish and Russian officials said. The Finnish Prime Minister warned that the war was spilling into the region.

A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday (November 20, 2026) night on Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said 60 people were wounded, including six children.
The strike caused four fires and damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles, Mr. Vilkul said.

Video footage published by the regional branch of the Ukrainian State Emergency Service appeared to show further strikes while ambulance and firefighting crews were responding at the scene, as fires burned around them.
“First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers, and utility workers,” Mr. Vilkul wrote on Telegram.

The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington. It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland, in what its Prime Minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

European troops were taking part on Friday (November 21, 2026) in an unprecedented two-week military exercise that began on November 9 in southeastern Poland. Forces are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilise the country and rebuild its military. European countries have previously expressed alarm at what they deem to be Russia's attempts to destabilise the continent.

At a meeting with U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv, Mr. Zelenskyy said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that Ukraine's repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland were a “fair response” to scores of Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges.
Mr. Zelenskyy said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that “Putin attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.”
“Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said. “This is important, that's why it's our absolutely fair response.”
The Ukrainian leader said that Mr. Putin “doesn't want to stop the war” and is looking to escalate. He also rejected Mr. Putin's claim that the Kerch bridge is used exclusively by civilian traffic.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The inability to reach compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participant country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries, and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels

Much like the 1.5 degree Celsius warming ceiling, COP31 proceedings under way at Antalya in Turkiye also breached upper limits with countries, as of Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, yet to behold a final text or convene a final plenary meeting to decide on the path forward for climate action.

Proceedings were expected to officially conclude on Friday (November 20, 2026), though historically it almost always goes into overtime and extends into the early hours of the weekend. The inability to reach a compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participating country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels and defining and paying out the trillions of dollars necessary to fund that transition as well as adapt to ongoing climate change.

The latest public iteration of the COP31 draft cover text, as of November 19, has eliminated references to fossil fuels phase out and net zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm US $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries.

Taking off from the previous editions of the COP in Baku, Azerbaijan and Belem, Brazil, developed nations said they would “take the lead” in contributing at least $300 billion annually towards mitigation and adaptation to climate change by 2035, though developing countries say this should be at least $ 1.3 trillion.

Other than the thorny debate on whether loans, grants, and for-profit investments in green projects are all included in this number, there is also debate on how much of the annual money should be split between adaptation and mitigation. The $120 billion was a proposal but that now has disappeared from the latest version of the text.
This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and scaling up the use of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) technologies. The latter involves unproven, expensive technology to extract atmospheric carbon dioxide. Proponents say this is necessary to counter the effects of the carbon that’s already in the atmosphere and responsible for the 1.5C temperature breach that has already occurred. To reiterate, the Paris Agreement goal is to keep temperatures below 2C and “as far as possible” below 1.5C. However, this has also been criticised by several civil society organisations as being an excuse to delay fossil-fuel phaseout.

“CC[U]S has been researched and developed for decades yet has achieved no discernible breakthroughs in efficiency, capture rates, or costs. Indeed, costs are getting higher. CCS is a tax on energy supplies at a time when affordability is strained and demand growth is seeking efficient supplies,” said Grant Hauber, Strategic Energy Finance Advisor, Asia, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) in a statement,” CO2 capture and disposal are a pure cost to the energy and production system.”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS), in a statement. “ Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

“The attempt to prove that a flashy headline target signals success for this COP has gone wrong in many ways for this Presidency,” said Avantika Goswami, Programme Manager, Centre for Science and Environment. “This text is a messy collation of disparate targets, some proposed as a menu of options, and some new decisions to establish new agendas. It lacks coherence and vision.”

articles.title: HPV vaccination: one crore doses administered in nine months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls has been covered under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign. Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh)

India has administered more than one crore doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months, covering nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign launched in February 2026, noted a release issued by the Union Health Ministry on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

It added that Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh). Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations.

The government provides the single-dose vaccine free of cost and voluntarily to eligible girls at designated government health facilities, with parental consent. The U-WIN digital platform facilitates beneficiary tracking, real-time monitoring, slot booking and digital certificates. Vaccination sessions are conducted under medical supervision, with arrangements for managing adverse events following immunisation, the Ministry said.
Among other high-performing States, Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, followed by Telangana (95.28%), Karnataka (93.16%) and Uttarakhand (90.17%).

Chhattisgarh (86.21%) and Rajasthan (85.23%) have crossed the 80% coverage mark, while Kerala (77.02%), Tamil Nadu (76.12%), Odisha (74.90%) and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (72.99%) have achieved more than 70% coverage.

In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads the country with more than 29.33 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with more than 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with more than 7.75 lakh girls vaccinated.

“School teachers, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) and other frontline healthcare workers have worked closely with parents and communities to encourage informed participation and counter misinformation,’’ the Ministry added.

It stated that digital health infrastructure has been an important enabler of the nationwide campaign, with the U-WIN platform supporting real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records.

The platform also enables parents to book HPV vaccination slots for their daughters and download digital vaccination certificates, making the vaccination process more accessible, convenient and transparent.

articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications

At least 13 people have died, and more than 300 have been hospitalised since November 18 after they consumed spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, police said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The patients are mostly from Chakpikarong and surrounding areas and have been hospitalised across multiple healthcare facilities in Imphal, including JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina Hospital.

"Thirteen people have been reported dead till 9 p.m. on Friday, while 346 patients have been admitted to hospitals due to suspected methanol poisoning, as they consumed spurious liquor," an official told PTI .
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospital and Babina Hospital on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026) to assess the situation and meet patients undergoing treatment.

In a social media post, Mr. Singh said, "Visited Shija Hospital at Lamphelpat, and Babina Hospital at Sajiwa, today [on Friday] to enquire about the health condition of the persons undergoing treatment after consuming spurious liquor from Chakpikarong area in Chandel District."
The Chandel district administration has intensified emergency response measures, and a team has been constituted for coordinated monitoring of the situation, an official notification said.
Four rapid response teams, equipped with adequate medicines and oxygen supplies, have been deployed in the district, the official said.

"Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours. The patients are undergoing medical evaluation and treatment under the close supervision of the doctors," he said.

"A medical team, led by a Specialist in General Medicine, along with essential medicines, has left for Chandel District to strengthen on-ground treatment and response", he said adding, "The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished."
Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan .K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications.
"Some patients are also undergoing hemodialysis", he added.
A JNIMS doctor said, "Many of the hospitalised include individuals who had consumed local liquor and had come to the hospital due to fear."

articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia.

The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya.

The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years.

The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years.

The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

2. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia.

Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

1. Core Context & Background: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War .
